title: [bug] Module ctx_memory advertises unusable mutations and leaves 9 facade tests red
description:
The module tool surface advertises five `ctx_memory` mutations that cannot work,
and this branch left nine facade tests failing on the vocabulary change.

The module schema offers `create`, `revise`, `archive`, `restore`, and `merge`
(`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:16942-16970`, enum at `:16948`) and the manifest
lists `ctx_memory` as a mutating tool (`prompt_surface.rs:206-211`,
`lib.rs:17025-17036`). Every one of those actions reaches a branch that
unconditionally returns `claim mutations require the host claim-operation commit
path` (`lib.rs:11341-11343`). A direct module or Claude Code call dispatches
straight to that handler (`lib.rs:10722`) with no host commit callback available,
so no advertised mutation can succeed on this surface.

Test evidence: `sh scripts/test-rust.sh` fails nine mc-module facade tests at
`e8b7640c`, all of which drive the pre-PR module vocabulary (`"action": "write"`,
`"action": "update"`):

- tests::draining_authority_rejects_every_facade_mutation_but_keeps_reads_resolved
- tests::facade_authority_lookup_failure_is_retryable_and_never_falls_back
- tests::facade_cache_mutations_drive_soft_memory_deltas_through_public_path
- tests::facade_merge_renders_a_budget_trimmed_target_then_defer_replays_bytes
- tests::facade_multi_instance_shares_memory_pool_and_splits_compartment_scope
- tests::facade_mutation_commands_replay_each_memory_and_note_action_without_advancing_state
- tests::facade_without_authority_keeps_path_scoped_writes
- tests::memory_facade_routes_all_authority_actions_into_store_and_changefeed
- tests::module_authority_facade_write_uses_identity_not_route_path

`origin/main` advertised `["write", "update", "archive", "merge", "get"]` and those
tests passed, so this branch replaced the vocabulary and removed the working
module-surface mutation path without updating or retiring its tests. Those nine
tests are exactly the end-to-end proof that module-surface memory mutation worked.

The decision is a product one, which is why this is a task rather than a fix:

- Relay module mutations through the staged host commit protocol, restore the
  tests against the new vocabulary, or
- advertise only the read actions on this surface and retire those tests with the
  capability.

Either way the suite must be green, and the manifest should not offer an action
that always errors.

Related read-surface divergence, same handler: module `get` and `list` read only
the auto-injection mirror, which is seeded with `surface: "auto_inject"` and active
lifecycle only (`claim-memory-render.ts:43-56`). The host `get` uses
`explicit_search` and additionally searches the caller's archived and retired
claims (`claim-actions.ts:335-376`); host `list` uses `explicit_search`
(`:405-420`). Explicit search keeps labeled stale, disputed, and superseded claims
that auto-injection rejects (`storage-claim-current-state.ts:373-413`). So an exact
module `get` reports no row for IDs that are valid and retrievable through the host
tool. Widening the auto-injection mirror is the wrong fix, because it would make
stale and explicit-only claims injectable; this needs its own explicit-search
projection.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (lib.rs:11343, lib.rs:11322) and coderabbit
(hook.ts:953, which is fixed on this branch).

title: [bug] MODULE-authority ctx_memory mutations always fail the staged-intent digest check
description:
Every `ctx_memory` mutation under MODULE memory authority fails after its context
write has already committed, because the staged intent's request digest and the
context receipt's request digest are computed over disjoint object shapes.

The stage side hashes the module-facing request built in
`packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-memory/tools.ts` (~163-194):
`{action, actor, projectIdentity, content?, category?, publicClaimId?,
publicClaimIds?, mutationToken?, mutationTokens?, reason?}`. That value reaches
`computeClaimOperationRequestDigest` through
`packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-wire.ts:656`.

The commit side reads `claim_operation_receipts.request_digest`, which each
operation computes from its own normalized input. For create that is
`packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claim-operations.ts:1204`:
`{actor, attributes, content, operation: "create-project-memory-claim",
projectId, provenance, requestScope, userInferred}`. Revise, lifecycle, and merge
use their own equally different shapes.

`computeClaimOperationRequestDigest` hashes the full canonical JSON of whatever
object it receives, with no field allowlist reconciling the two vocabularies, so
the two digests can never be equal. `commitModuleClaimIntent`
(`packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/context-authority.ts:220`) compares
them and throws `context receipt digest does not match staged claim intent`.

The throw happens after `args.commitContext()` at line 213, so the claim is
already durably written to context.db. The caller sees a failure for a completed
write, and the intent stays unresolved, which blocks `begin_claim_store_rebuild`
and `replace_claim_mirror_snapshot`.

Independently reported by three reviewers on PR #38: codex (tools.ts:168),
claude (context-authority.ts:220), coderabbit (tools.ts:194).

Two candidate resolutions, and the choice is a protocol decision:

Option A, share one canonical request builder. Hoist input normalization out of
`packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-memory/claim-actions.ts` so the tool can build the
same normalized request the operation will use, then stage a digest over that.
This keeps the digest a genuine end-to-end fence but touches four operations and
their normalization (`resolveAttributes`, `provenanceRequestShape`, numeric
`projectId` resolution).

Option B, stop comparing across vocabularies. Drop the digest equality check and
rely on the identity assertion already present at
`context-authority.ts:214-219`, which compares `producer` and `operationKey` —
the receipt's primary key, derived identically on both sides by
`createCtxMemoryProducerIdentity`. Reuse of one tool-call ID with different
arguments is already fenced twice, each within a single vocabulary:
`stage_claim_intent` on the module side and `runClaimOperation`
(`storage-claim-operations.ts:429-440`) on the context side.

Option B is the smaller change and loses no fence that currently holds. Option A
is the stronger contract. Either way the crash-recovery tests need a case whose
`commit.requestDigest` is produced by a real operation rather than rebuilt from
the staged object, since `context-authority-crash.test.ts:137` currently derives
both digests from the same value and masks the mismatch.

title: Daemon routes + TS thin client
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — U1; R1, R3, R5, R8, R10; KTD1, KTD5; Kernel Design Baseline.

## Goal
Expose kernel operations through `mc-module` hosted by `magic-contextd`, and replace direct TypeScript storage access with thin clients.

## Scope
- Kernel write, read, and eligibility-batch routes.
- OpenCode, Pi, and Desktop clients call daemon routes instead of implementing kernel logic.
- Eligibility validation accepts candidate IDs and indexed source revisions, batch-loads canonical state, and rejects retracted, stale, wrong-scope, superseded, or provider-sensitive candidates before reranking or injection.
- Eligibility cache keys include `core_commit_seq`.
- Daemon absence returns explicit memory-unavailable behavior. Do not retain a TS fallback pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Route and client tests prove daemon-authoritative writes, complete known_as_of reads, canonical batch eligibility, core_commit_seq cache invalidation, and explicit unavailable behavior when the daemon is down; static checks find no parallel TS kernel or memory-search fallback.

title: core.sqlite kernel store
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — U1; R1–R6, R10; KTD1, KTD5, KTD6; Kernel Design Baseline.

## Goal
Implement the Rust-owned `core.sqlite` kernel in `crates/mc-store`, following the existing `sqlite_runtime.rs` open gate and single-writer pattern.

## Scope
- Envelope: `commit_log`, `change_event`, and `outbox`.
- Kernel: object registry, domains, entities and aliases, propositions, predicate schemas, scopes, anchors, evidence metadata, and asserted edges.
- Staging: extraction runs, candidates, scores, and admission decisions.
- Initial slice: decisions, decision events, observations, and observation dependencies.
- Rebuildable core projection: alignment.
- One transaction and `commit_seq` per canonical mutation, atomic outbox publication, idempotency keys, and complete `known_as_of` snapshots.
- One full schema shape with no migration chain, compatibility shim, dual read, or backfill.
- Port the direct-format identity vocabulary: `MCTX` application ID, format marker, pristine-or-exact open, quarantine, and discard-and-rebuild.
- Use WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, strict tables, foreign keys, `trusted_schema=OFF`, no runtime extension loading, short transactions, and online backup.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh open creates the complete core schema; mismatched identity is quarantined and rebuilt; transaction and fault tests prove one commit_seq, atomic changes/outbox, idempotent replay, and complete known_as_of reads; no migration or compatibility path exists; SQLite safety-profile tests pass.

title: artifacts/ CAS store
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — U1; R2, R5, R10; KTD5; Kernel Design Baseline.

## Goal
Implement durable content-addressed evidence storage under `artifacts/`.

## Scope
- Write temp file → hash and fsync → atomic rename into CAS → commit canonical reference.
- Never create a canonical reference before artifact durability.
- Store retention, sensitivity, redaction, and provider-egress metadata.
- Garbage-collect unreferenced objects within K1 budgets.
- Propagate deletion to derived support, retrieval documents, embeddings, and admission state, with explicit backfill barriers.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection proves canonical state never references an undurable artifact; hashes deduplicate bytes; retention and GC preserve referenced objects; deletion emits complete propagation work and backfill barriers; sensitive artifacts cannot leave their allowed provider boundary.

title: Scope algebra + anchor engine
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — U1; R3–R5, R7–R8; KTD5; Kernel Design Baseline. This task absorbs the engine design from `magic-context-3q5.40`.

## Scope algebra
Support bounded dimensions for domain, project/repo, entity/component, branch/worktree, environment, region, deployment/version, request class, caller class, and provider/platform. Support exact match, set membership, version range, git reachability, and unspecified/all. Implement deterministic `scope_matches`, `scope_overlaps`, `scope_subsumes`, and `scope_equivalent`.

## Anchors and effective conditions
Support `Exact(anchor)`, `ReachableFrom(oid)`, `ReachableBetween(start, end)`, `DeploymentRevision`, `ConfigRevision`, `PlatformVersion(range)`, and `WallClockInterval`. Treat git history as a DAG.

## Applicability engine and retrieval-time read repair
- Resolve introduced and invalidated anchors against current HEAD using merge-base ancestry.
- Use patch-ID fallback for rebases and cherry-picks; use tree or symbol-hash fallback when commits are unavailable.
- Classify overlap between uncommitted paths and affected paths as `dirty_tree_uncertain`.
- Run bounded cheap checks for file existence, symbol resolution, and config-key presence.
- Keep work cancellable and deadline-checked. Cache results per `(anchor, HEAD, dirty-fingerprint)` generation and never spawn a git subprocess per candidate or on a cache hit.
- On failed cheap checks, mark the object stale or uncertain, append a verification/invalidation event, schedule deep verification, and prevent automatic injection immediately.
- Keep historical and uncertain results available only through labeled explicit search.
- Conflict and supersession remain evidence-bundle concerns; this engine determines repository-state applicability.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests cover all four scope predicates; fixture repositories distinguish current, historical, invalidated, and dirty_tree_uncertain states; rebase and cherry-pick fixtures prove patch-ID fallback; work remains bounded and cancellable; cache hits spawn zero git subprocesses; failed read repair records invalidation and blocks the same object from automatic injection without waiting for deep verification; all state changes are atomic under known_as_of.

title: Admission + visibility on kernel
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — U1; R4–R5, R7–R8; KTD5.

## Goal
Re-express v86 admission and visibility semantics on kernel objects without retaining the TS claims implementation.

## Scope
- Maturity ladder: CANDIDATE → CORROBORATED → VERIFIED → APPROVED → ENFORCED.
- Table-driven source-taint classes, promotion rules, and visibility matrix.
- Staging candidates remain invisible to canonical retrieval and automatic prompt injection until admission.
- Automatic admission is deterministic and narrow: explicit rejection, correction, or replacement; accepted ADR; positive code or configuration observation.
- Support explicit rejection, correction, and replacement as append-only events.
acceptance_criteria: One table-driven evaluator governs admission and visibility; promotion tests enforce taint limits; unadmitted staging objects never enter canonical retrieval or prompt injection; only listed deterministic source classes can auto-admit; rejection, correction, and replacement preserve prior canonical history.
notes: Residue transferred from magic-context-3q5.32: kernel writers must require explicit source/taint classification; do not preserve the TS fallback to model_inference.

title: epic: Semantic kernel and truth maintenance
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` — Goal Capsule; R1–R10; R14; KTD1, KTD3, KTD5, KTD6; Kernel Design Baseline.

## Goal
Build one Rust-native semantic kernel owned by `magic-contextd`. The daemon is the only memory writer and semantic authority; OpenCode, Pi, and Desktop are thin clients; daemon absence makes memory unavailable.

## Architecture
- Store canonical state, staging, commit log, and outbox in `core.sqlite`; durable evidence in `artifacts/`; rebuildable retrieval documents and FTS5 in `search.sqlite`; measured, model-versioned embeddings in `vectors/`.
- Commit every canonical mutation through one transactional `commit_seq`; make `known_as_of` reads atomic; project outbox events asynchronously and idempotently.
- Provide typed object, proposition, predicate, entity, scope, anchor, evidence, and asserted-edge primitives without imposing shared truth semantics across object kinds.
- Keep staging invisible before admission and derived state rebuildable from canonical state.
- Create one full schema shape. Quarantine and rebuild mismatches; do not add migrations, compatibility paths, dual reads, or backfills.
- Re-express v86 maturity, taint, visibility, bitemporal, and git-applicability semantics on the kernel while deleting their TS claims/mirror implementation.
- Prove the decision → observation → alignment slice and every R8 correctness obligation.
- Include retention, sensitivity, redaction, provider-egress, and durable CAS rules from the first schema.
- Defer hypotheses, episodes, policy sets, topics, and procedure automation under R9.

## Ownership
This epic owns kernel and truth-maintenance work. `magic-context-3q5` remains the separate retrieval, benchmark, and vector-engine lane consuming kernel stores.
acceptance_criteria: K1–K10 are complete; every R8 proof passes; magic-contextd is the sole memory authority; kernel storage, admission, scope, CAS, and thin-client behavior satisfy R1–R10; replaced TS/Rust claims machinery is removed; KD1–KD4 remain deferred; retrieval and vector work remains under magic-context-3q5.

title: Project config can enable bash-capable dreamer maintain-docs task
description:
Untrusted project config can enable a shell-capable unattended dreamer task.

`project-security.ts` strips only `prompt`/`permission`/`tools`/`system_prompt`
from hidden-agent blocks. `dreamer.disable` and `dreamer.tasks.*.schedule` are
deliberately left unstripped so a repo can tune its own dreamer cadence, and the
header comment says so. The residual risk that comment does not cover:

- `maintain-docs` ships disabled (default schedule `""`,
  packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts:188) and the schema accepts
  any five-field cron, including `* * * * *`.
- It runs as `dreamer-docs`, whose allowlist includes `bash`, `write`, `edit`
  (packages/plugin/src/agents/hidden-agent-registrations.ts:141). The Pi path has
  the same allowlist and merges the parent environment into the child.
- `isDreamerRunnable` is just `!!config.dreamer && config.dreamer.disable !== true`
  (packages/plugin/src/config/agent-disable.ts:11), and project values merge over
  user values, so a repo can also undo a user's `dreamer.disable: true`.
- The `maintain-docs` activity gate only requires a new compartment since the last
  run. No per-run approval.

So a repo committing `.cortexkit/magic-context.jsonc` with
`{"dreamer":{"disable":false,"tasks":{"maintain-docs":{"schedule":"* * * * *"}}}}`
turns on an unattended bash-capable pass over repo-controlled files. Exploitation
still needs indirect prompt injection in a file the docs pass reads AND model
compliance, so severity is Medium, not High. The task prompt's "only write these
two docs, don't read credentials" is model prose, not a host boundary, and the
post-run protected-region restore cannot undo shell side effects.

Remediation options:
1. Treat `dreamer.disable` and every `dreamer.tasks.*.schedule` as user-tier-only;
   strip them from project config.
2. Or require a one-time user approval showing task name, cadence, tool set, and
   working-directory scope before a project-proposed schedule can enable a task
   with `bash`/`write`/`edit`.
3. Enforce the docs task's authority in the host, not in prose.
4. Regression tests: untrusted project config cannot turn a disabled task
   runnable, cannot override a trusted `dreamer.disable: true`, and cannot supply
   a nonempty schedule for a shell-capable task.

Provenance: recovered from a deleted security-audit working directory
(`piolium/`, finding M1) so the finding survives the directory's removal. The
audit's PoC was source-grounded only (no model-backed execution), which is why
the original write-up graded itself inconclusive on end-to-end impact.

title: Benchmark bounded Synapse inference slices
description: Prototype only the smallest candidate from magic-context-1fc: keep one Backend, one FIFO CPU semaphore, and current admission; split each admitted batch job into bounded inference slices and re-acquire the same permit between slices so queued queries can run. Before production code, use the exact qualified gte-modernbert-base-f16 bundle and ORT on supported linux-x64. Measure single-row query and batch slice service for rows {1,2,4,8,16}, intra-op threads {1,2,4}, mixed 16/64-item jobs, token-length strata, query p99/deadline success, batch goodput, CPU, host-only RSS, shutdown drain, and vector parity. Reject dynamic-quantized slicing. Adopt only a fixed private slice width/thread count that improves query deadline success without worse batch goodput, query outcome rates, RSS bound, or shutdown in every fresh-process pair. Experiment harness stays disposable; final diff keeps only selected production code, focused invariant tests, and decision record. Coordinate input validation/tokenization seam with magic-context-chj; do not add model pools, EDF, cross-request coalescing, or public knobs.

title: Research optimal Synapse mixed-load inference
description: Find an evidence-backed production architecture that improves interactive query tails under batch indexing load beyond the rejected T2 class-arbitration design. Compare preemption/chunking, bounded model pools, ORT threading/batching, and workload shaping against current mc-host invariants, memory bounds, deadlines, shutdown, and release constraints. Produce a recommendation, switch conditions, implementation outline, and benchmark contract; do not implement.
notes: Research complete. Primary recommendation: bounded batch work-unit slicing with one existing Backend/session and unchanged FIFO semaphore. Re-acquire CPU permit between slices; validate whole job once; accumulate and publish once; check closing/lane failure at each boundary; dynamic quantization must remain one call. Benchmark exact production gte-modernbert-base-f16 + ORT before code, slice rows {1,2,4,8,16}, intra-op {1,2,4}. Fallback only if slicing fails: two dedicated sessions after host-only RSS/core-isolation proof. Reject T2-only arbitration, cross-request coalescing, process isolation, and speculative model pools. Follow-up magic-context-w4g, blocked by c50.8 and related to chj.
close_reason: Evidence-backed recommendation and benchmark handoff completed; follow-up tracked by magic-context-w4g

title: Retrieval benchmark baselines/v1 no longer matches main; the quality gate fails identically everywhere
description:
## Problem

`Benchmark (retrieval, deterministic CI profile)` fails its "Gate quality against
published ci baseline" step against `packages/plugin/scripts/fixtures/retrieval-benchmark/baselines/v1`:

    quality: automatic ndcgAt10 loss avg=50.000 worst=50.000 points
    quality: automatic recallAt50 loss avg=50.000 worst=50.000 points
    quality: explicit recallAt50 loss avg=23.214 worst=23.214 points

Baseline means are 1.0 for both automatic metrics; candidates measure 0.5.
Explicit recallAt50 is 0.964 baseline against 0.732 measured. The policy allows
2pp.

## This is not caused by PR 78

Ran the `check` three times plus the `regression` gate at four commits. Every one
produces byte-identical losses:

| commit | what it is | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` (9ee79e21) | main tip | policy-fail, same numbers |
| `e1c756fb` | PR 78 head before any review fixes | policy-fail, same numbers |
| `bebdb563` | PR 78 after review fixes, before the main merge | policy-fail, same numbers |
| `e12d484d` | PR 78 after the merge | policy-fail, same numbers |

Identical on main means the published baseline no longer describes main's
retrieval behaviour. The gate is path-gated, so it is SKIPPED on main's own CI
runs and only fires on a PR that touches retrieval paths — which is why it went
unnoticed and why it looks like PR 78's fault.

Reproduce:

    for i in 1 2 3; do
      bun packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-retrieval.ts check --profile ci \
        --out /tmp/r$i.json
    done
    b=packages/plugin/scripts/fixtures/retrieval-benchmark/baselines/v1
    bun packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-retrieval.ts regression \
      --baseline "$b/quality.json" --policy "$b/policy.json" \
      --candidate /tmp/r1.json --candidate /tmp/r2.json --candidate /tmp/r3.json \
      --out /tmp/reg.json

## What has to be decided

Either main regressed retrieval quality at some point and the baseline is the
honest record of what was lost, or the baseline was ratified against a corpus,
judgment set, or embedding profile that has since changed and needs
re-ratification. The report carries `releaseFingerprints` for corpus, judgments,
synthetic profiles, and manifest; comparing those against the ones the baseline
was ratified under separates the two cases and should be the first step.

Until it is settled, the gate cannot distinguish a real ranking regression from
this standing offset, so it blocks every retrieval-touching PR for a reason none
of them caused.

## Acceptance

- The fingerprint comparison is recorded, naming which side moved.
- Either the baseline is re-ratified with evidence, or the quality loss on main
  is traced to the change that caused it and fixed.
- The gate runs on main, not only on PRs, so the next drift is attributed to the
  commit that caused it.

title: Shadow embedding measurement compares a shadow query vector against primary passage vectors
description:
## Problem

`runShadowEmbeddingMeasurement` overrides `embedQuery` with a vector from
`embedShadowTextForProject`, but leaves `embedPassages` unset:

    packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search-measurement.ts:46-61

`unifiedSearch` then falls back to its default passage embedder, which calls
`embedBatchForProject` (the project's PRIMARY provider) and validates the batch
against the primary generation and model id:

    packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts:2105-2116

So the anti-memory semantic lane scores a shadow-model query against
primary-model passages. Differing dimensions score zero, which silently removes
the lane from the shadow ranking; equal dimensions produce a meaningless
cross-model similarity. Either way the recorded shadow result ids and corpus
hash do not describe the model being measured, so a model-swap decision reads
off corrupted evidence.

Scope is telemetry only: the shadow run sets `measurementDisabled` and
`countRetrievals: false`, so no user-facing result and no retrieval counter is
affected.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #78 (P1) and confirmed by reading the
code.

## Why it was not fixed in the PR review pass

There is no shadow batch embedder. `embedShadowTextForProject` is single-text,
so the options are:

1. Add a shadow batch API alongside `embedBatchForProject` and pass it as
   `embedPassages` during shadow search. Correct, but a new provider entry
   point with its own generation and model-id validation.
2. Fan out `embedShadowTextForProject` per passage (bounded by
   `ANTI_MEMORY_MAX_SEMANTIC_CANDIDATES`, so at most 32 calls). Cheap to write,
   but 32 sequential provider calls per shadow search on a telemetry path.
3. Supply `embedPassages: async (texts) => texts.map(() => null)` so shadow runs
   are lexical-only for anti-memory. Removes the corruption but makes the shadow
   and primary rankings incomparable for that lane, which defeats the point of
   the measurement.

Picking among these is a measurement-design decision, not a review fix.

## Acceptance

- A shadow search either embeds passages with the shadow model contract or is
  documented as excluding the semantic anti-memory lane, with the exclusion
  visible in the recorded measurement rather than implicit in a zero score.
- A test asserts the passage vectors a shadow run consumes come from the same
  model contract as its query vector.

title: Anti-memory warnings are lost on every transform pass after the one that created the decision
description:
## Problem

`autoSearchHintFragmentsStillEligible` returns `fragments.length === 0`, so a
persisted auto-search decision that carries anti-memory fragments never
replays. That is deliberate: warning text must be re-derived, not replayed from
storage.

The suppression half is implemented; the re-derivation half is not. In
`runAutoSearchHint` the existing-decision branch suppresses the text and
returns immediately:

    packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/auto-search-runner.ts:316-321
      const existingForMessage = existing.find((d) => d.messageId === userMsgId);
      if (existingForMessage) {
          replayHintIfEligible(existingForMessage);   // suppressed, no-op
          return AUTO_SEARCH_OK;                      // no fresh search
      }

So the warning reaches the model only on the pass that created the decision.
Every later transform pass over the same user message drops it. That the
messages array is rebuilt per pass is evident from `replayHintIfEligible`
itself: ordinary hints must be re-appended each pass, and
`appendReminderToUserMessageById` is not idempotent
(`transform-message-helpers.ts:54`), so nothing survives a pass on its own.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #78 (P1) and confirmed by reading
the code.

## Why it was not fixed in the PR review pass

The fix is a protocol change, not a local patch:

1. The early return must fall through to a fresh search when the persisted
   decision is a non-replayable warning.
2. The delivery condition
   (`outcome.kind === "appended" && warningResults.length > 0`,
   auto-search-runner.ts:466) must also deliver on an `already-present` CAS
   outcome, since the second pass necessarily loses the CAS.
3. Re-derived text is not guaranteed byte-identical to the first pass, so a
   non-tail pass can bust the provider cache the tail gate
   (auto-search-runner.ts:333) exists to protect. Either accept the bust for
   warnings or accept single-pass delivery — that is a product decision.
4. `recordDeliveredAntiMemoryUsage` would fire once per delivering pass;
   decide whether usage counts deliveries or turns.

Five call sites share the suppression shape and must agree:

  - packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/auto-search-runner.ts:306
  - packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/transform-postprocess-phase.ts:399
  - packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/transform-postprocess-phase.ts:1729
  - packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-state-sync.ts:963
  - packages/pi-plugin/src/auto-search-pi.ts:279
  - packages/pi-plugin/src/context-handler.ts:5779

## Acceptance

- A second transform pass over a user message whose decision carries
  anti-memory fragments either delivers a freshly derived warning or is
  documented as intentionally single-pass, with a test for whichever is chosen.
- The chosen rule holds identically in the OpenCode and Pi harnesses.
- The cache-bust and usage-counting decisions are recorded in the code as
  mechanism comments.

title: Pair-only anti-memory dedup can launder explicit-user trust onto a model-authored reason
description:
Found in review of PR #77 and confirmed against the code. Not fixed there: the
fix changes trust-classification semantics, which wants its own change and tests.

## Mechanism

`antiMemoryDedupText` keys only the PAIR:

    JSON.stringify([payload.trigger, payload.rejectedStrategy])

so two corrections that share a trigger and rejected strategy collide even when
`rejectionReason`, `saferAlternative`, and the rest differ.

On collision, `stageCreateProjectMemoryClaimInCurrentTransaction` takes the dedup
branch and calls `attachEvidenceStage`, which appends a `claim_evidence` row
against the EXISTING revision and preserves the existing payload.

`hasExplicitUserEvidence` (storage-claim-policy.ts:509) accepts any
`explicit_user` supporting observation when `cr.revision = 1`.

Compose those:

1. The harvest creates a model-inferred anti-memory. Revision 1 holds reason A.
2. A later correction shares trigger and rejected strategy but carries reason B,
   and IS corroborated, so the harvest supplies `sourceTrustClass:
   'explicit_user'`.
3. Dedup attaches that explicit-user observation to revision 1 and keeps reason A.
4. `hasExplicitUserEvidence(revision 1)` is now true, so reason A is classified as
   explicitly user-supported.

The user corroborated reason B. Reason A was never user-supported, and it is the
text that stays durable and gets the trust.

## Why it is not a one-liner

Three shapes, each with a real cost:

- Include the full payload in the dedup text. Different wording of the same
  warning then creates separate claims, which is the duplication the pair key
  exists to prevent.
- Revise the existing claim to the corroborated payload. That is the append-a-
  revision problem tracked in magic-context-xqg: expiry and payload live in
  append-only per-revision rows, so it needs a minted token,
  `antiMemoryWriter: true`, an `insertPayload` for the new revision, and merged
  stage outcomes.
- Refuse the trust upgrade on the dedup path: attach the observation as
  `model_inference` when the incoming payload differs from the stored one. Least
  invasive and fails closed, but it needs the harvest to know it deduped BEFORE
  the observation is written, and today the trust class is chosen before staging.

The third is probably right, and pairs naturally with magic-context-xqg since both
concern what the dedup branch should do with a newer, better correction.

## Acceptance

- A corroborated correction that dedups onto a claim with a DIFFERENT stored
  payload must not leave that claim reading as explicitly user-supported.
- A corroborated correction whose payload matches the stored one may still
  attach explicit-user evidence.
- Existing pair dedup behaviour for identical payloads is unchanged.

title: Three CI jobs were skipped behind a red gate on main and are failing when un-gated
description:
`check-plugin` has been failing on every recent main run, and three jobs declare
`needs: [check-plugin]`, so they have been SKIPPED rather than run:

- Benchmark (retrieval, deterministic CI profile)
- Incident regression pool (supported TS)
- E2E (OpenCode, host behavior)

Confirmed skipped on main runs 33129589712, 33129500202, 33118782478.

PR #77 fixes the deterministic `check-plugin` failure, which un-gates all three,
and all three fail. None of the failures are caused by that PR.

## Benchmark (retrieval): pre-existing, proven

`verdict=policy-fail` against the published v1 baseline:

    quality: automatic ndcgAt10  loss avg=50.000 worst=50.000 points
    quality: automatic recallAt50 loss avg=50.000 worst=50.000 points
    quality: explicit  recallAt50 loss avg=23.214 worst=23.214 points

Reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree (1a969c8f) with the same three-run
CI recipe. The verdict and all three loss figures are byte-identical to the PR
branch, and both produce the same `semanticFingerprint`
`2084bd935e8701472e1b3c2f64c335020102856edccfafe20d38396933a3c0a1`, so retrieval
semantics are unchanged between them.

Either retrieval quality regressed on main while this gate was skipped, or the v1
baseline no longer describes current behaviour. Needs a decision on which.

## Incident regression pool: unrelated subsystem

    mutations/shm-hardening-u1.json.mutations[0]: cannot resolve a verifier from
    command "cargo test -p mc-shm-transport --test iceoryx
    allocation_slack_never_reaches_the_frame_decoder"

A mutation-bound verifier pointing at an mc-shm-transport test that no longer
resolves. SHM hardening, nothing to do with memory or claims.

## E2E (OpenCode, host behavior): mostly the U8 leftovers

- `Cannot find module '.../memory/storage-memory-claims'` and
  `no project-memory claim matching "test seeded directive: ..."` are the same
  incomplete f4ee5460 migration already tracked in magic-context-6wr.
- `packages/pi-plugin/dist/index.js is missing. Run: cd packages/pi-plugin &&
  bun run build` looks like a missing build step in this job, since the OpenCode
  job exercises a cross-harness parity test that needs the Pi bundle.
- `synthetic todowrite e2e > clears the persisted synthetic anchor when the
  latest todo state is terminal-only` expects 1 and receives 3; unrelated to
  memory.

## Why this matters beyond the individual failures

A red required gate has been hiding three downstream gates. Whatever order these
get fixed in, `check-plugin` should be kept green, or the same masking recurs.

title: CI red on main: e2e-tests still import storage removed by the U8 legacy-memory retirement
description:
Two CI jobs fail on main itself, not only on PRs. Confirmed on run 33129589712
(sha 1a969c8f, main tip): `Prospective release holdout contracts` and
`E2E (Pi, host behavior)` both fail, and they fail identically on every branch
that merges current main.

Shared root cause: commit f4ee5460 ("remove the retired memory storage now that
claims are the supported kernel and rewire remaining consumers to the claim
APIs") deleted the legacy memory storage but left three consumers in
packages/e2e-tests importing symbols and tables that no longer exist.

## Prospective release holdout contracts

`packages/e2e-tests/src/incident-pool/scenarios/audit-memory-search.ts:28`
imports `withClaimsWriteCapabilityInCurrentTransaction` from
`plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory-claims`. That module
was deleted in f4ee5460 and the symbol exists nowhere in source, so the module
fails to resolve and takes 4 tests down as unhandled errors.

Not an import-path fix. The wrapper gated writes on
`claim_compatibility_write_state`, a compatibility table that is also gone, and
the body it wraps does
`UPDATE memories SET content = ... WHERE id = ?` against the retired `memories`
table. `storage-format-epoch.test.ts:791` explicitly asserts `memories` and
`claim_compatibility_write_state` are ABSENT from a fresh schema. The scenario is
written against storage that no longer exists.

Two sibling references to the same dead path need the same decision:
- audit-memory-search.ts:317
- audit-memory-search.test.ts:529 and :532

## E2E (Pi, host behavior)

`packages/e2e-tests/src/oracle-arms/seed-gold-memories.ts:3` imports
`getMemoryById`, which is no longer exported from
`plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/index.ts`:

    SyntaxError: Export named 'getMemoryById' not found in module ...

The seeding helper inserts a legacy memory and reads it back by id, so it has the
same problem: it seeds storage that was retired.

Two further failures in that job are downstream of the same seeding path:
- pi memory injection > injects <project-memory> into the Pi system prompt
- pi cross harness > shares public-tool project memory writes between OpenCode
  and Pi both directions

Both fail with `no project-memory claim matching "..." found`, i.e. the gold
memories never got seeded.

## Decision needed

Each scenario is either ported onto the claim APIs (seed project-memory claims
instead of legacy `memories` rows, drop the compatibility wrapper, which is
unnecessary now that claims are the kernel) or retired with its coverage moved.
That is a judgement about what these scenarios are meant to prove, which belongs
with the U8 cutover rather than an unrelated feature branch.

Noticed while getting PR #77 green. The third main-red job, `Check (plugin)`, had
a different cause and is fixed on that branch.

title: PR #49 review: harden generation store, spawn, and lifecycle CLI
description:
Address verified review findings on PR #49 (stack/mc-host-03-native-runtime) from coderabbitai, chatgpt-codex-connector, and kilo-code-bot.

Verified-valid findings being fixed:
- generation.rs: open_verified_file returns an EOF-positioned descriptor (dup shares the offset)
- generation.rs: available_bytes multiplies f_bavail by f_bsize instead of f_frsize
- generation.rs: persisted manifests are not required to use the canonical encoding
- generation.rs: unlisted-entry walk re-resolves the pathname instead of the retained descriptor
- generation.rs: oversized manifests are promoted and selected before the read cap rejects them
- generation.rs: renameat replaces an empty protected digest directory before the protection check
- generation.rs: ENOSPC surfaced by fsync is misclassified as native_payload_invalid
- generation.rs: nested staged directories are never fsynced before promotion
- generation.rs: the lifecycle root is created through pathname mkdir, so intermediate symlinks are followed
- generation.rs: open_probe maps every generations-directory open failure to Ok(None)
- ck-mc-host.rs: probe emits a command outside the release contract's closed union
- ck-mc-host.rs: authenticate can overrun the spawn/publication phase deadline
- ck-mc-host.rs: a non-UTF-8 data root panics through expect instead of failing closed
- spawn.rs: a restrictive umask can leave daemon.log mode 000 and pass the security check
- spawn.rs: the pre-5.9 close fallback ceiling leaks descriptors at or above 8192
- spawn.rs: inherited signal dispositions and the signal mask survive into the daemon
- serve.rs: the SIGTERM stream is installed inside a spawned task, racing host startup
- tests/support/synapse.rs: open_synapse_route_rejection returns module_reloading on timeout

title: Scrub internal dev-host identifiers from .beads/issues.jsonl (public repo)
description:
ahrav/magic-context is a public GitHub repository, and .beads/issues.jsonl on
main contains internal Amazon development-host names, for example
dev-dsk-ahrav-2b-7dc7bd93.us-west-2.amazon.com,
dev-dsk-ahrav-2b-a030d1dc.us-west-2.amazon.com, and
dev-dsk-ahrav-2c-a9191cb6.us-west-2.amazon.com.

Found while reviewing PR 68. That PR redacted the same identifier class from the
retained perf evidence bundles under docs/perf/runs/ (hostname replaced with
"<redacted: collection host>", absolute paths with "<repo>"), but deliberately
did not touch .beads/issues.jsonl: it is bd-managed state, so scrubbing it needs
to go through bd rather than a text edit, and it is outside that PR's scope.

Work:
- Identify every record carrying a hostname or an absolute /local/home path.
- Rewrite those fields through bd so the database stays consistent.
- Check whether anything else in .beads leaks host or account identifiers.
- Consider preventing recurrence, since these values appear to arrive from
  automated capture of a working environment rather than being typed by hand.

Note that the identifiers are already in public git history, so a scrub of the
current file limits further exposure but does not undo it. Decide separately
whether history rewriting is warranted.

title: Synapse tail: next epoch must validate schedule identity, block-paired contrasts, and post-exclusion selection inputs
description:
Review of PR 68 found three defects in the retained synapse-tail epoch tooling
(docs/perf/runs/synapse-tail-881be45b/). Those scripts are immutable evidence
artifacts covered by the bundle SHA256SUMS, so they were not edited; the
limitations are recorded in that bundle's report under "Post-collection
redaction and retained-tooling limits". The fixes belong to the next collection
epoch's scripts.

Requirements for the next epoch:

1. Schedule identity. analyze.py derives phase completeness from the number of
   status files without binding each status record to a planned schedule entry,
   so a duplicated status record plus a missing planned position passes the
   completeness check. Index planned entries by (sequence, cell) and require
   exactly one matching status record per entry before claiming completeness.

2. Block-paired contrasts. select.py averages candidate and hygiene-only rows
   independently and never joins on `block`, so a contrast can be an unpaired
   aggregate. The 881be45b run has single-valid-block treatment cells where this
   is the case. Join on `block`, emit only matched-block ratios, and label or
   exclude anything unpaired.

3. Post-exclusion selection inputs. analyze.py writes
   analysis/valid-cell-summaries.csv from unfiltered raw summaries, and select.py
   consumes it, so the selection inputs, contrast table, and queue objective all
   predate the warm-state exclusion. Compute selection inputs from post-warmup
   summaries.

4. Output directories. run_matrix.py writes into ROOT/phase/raw and ROOT/phase
   without creating them, so a clean-checkout re-run fails before any cell
   executes. Create them in execute() and before the calibration and schedule
   writes.

5. Emit the hold boundaries. The 881be45b harness took its closed-loop hold
   origin before spawning workers and never emitted it, so the warmup
   re-analysis had to reconstruct it from the earliest observed send and is
   approximate in a known direction. The current harness emits
   hold_window_start_ns, warmup_end_ns, hold_window_end_ns, and a per-row window
   class, so a new epoch can apply the frozen exclusion exactly.

6. Host build identity. baseline and hygiene-only cells are only pre-change host
   code when the harness itself was built at the pinned pre-change commit. Build
   with MC_HOST_PERF_BUILD_ID set and record the id plus its commit in the run
   manifest; the harness now refuses those variants from an unidentified build.

Consequence: the a+c K=1 selection stays provisional until an epoch satisfies 1,
2, 3, and 5. That cannot be resolved by re-analyzing the retained run.

title: [bug] Authority transitions never write their claim-intent control row
description:
`set_claim_intent_transition_tx` silently ignores the identity the host actually
has, so authority transitions never record their control row.

The helper accepts only 32 lowercase hex characters and otherwise returns `Ok(())`
without writing (`crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs:5990-5998`). All four callers pass
`context_store_uuid`:

- `authority_begin_prepare` (`:15462-15467`)
- `authority_finish_prepare` (`:15681-15690`)
- both `authority_begin_drain` branches (`:15779-15784`, `:15831-15836`)

`ensureContextStoreUuid` persists a hyphenated `randomUUID()`
(`packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/context-authority.ts:418-438`), which
is 36 characters. The direct incarnation marker is a separately generated 16 random
bytes as 32 lowercase hex (`storage-format-epoch.ts:59-78`) and is what the claim
binding carries (`hook.ts:921-965`). The two identities are independently random,
so stripping hyphens is not a conversion.

Result: every production transition is a no-op against
`mc_claim_intent_controls`, so the durable transition state is never recorded. That
is the same control row the mirror depends on for `resetting` and `draining`
(`claim_mirror.rs:784-820`, `915-925`), which is why the mirror has no reachable
rebuild path.

Scope correction against the original report: staging is not left unfenced. As of
`e8b7640c`, stage resolves authority through the bound route
(`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:10757-10775`, `crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs:5965-5988`)
and rejects a missing authority, a non-`MODULE` state, a wrong project, or a wrong
generation (`:15082-15104`). Tests cover PREPARING and DRAINING
(`crates/mc-store/tests/claim_intent_ledger.rs:168-214`). The live defect is the
unrecorded control row, not an accepted intent during a transition.

Wanted: carry the direct database incarnation through authority transitions
alongside the store UUID so the control row is written, and make an unusable
identity an error rather than a silent `Ok(())`. Check `authority_ack_prepare` for
the same gap.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (mc-store/src/lib.rs:15012) and coderabbit
(mc-store/src/lib.rs:6017).

title: Page claim-mirror snapshots and receipts under the facade frame cap
description:
Claim-mirror facade calls are capped at 1 MiB, and neither the full snapshot nor a
receipt group is paged, so a project with enough claims fails every sync pass and
suppresses the claim lane permanently.

`enforce_request_byte_cap` keeps a 1 MiB default and a 32 MiB transform cap
(`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:15166-15171`), and grants the larger cap only to
`kind=transform` or `method=state_sync` (`:15184-15191`, enforced `:15262-15277`).
Claim bodies are addressed by a top-level `name`, not `method`
(`packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-wire.ts:626-643`), so they get
1 MiB.

`claimMirrorReplace` sends one complete snapshot
(`module-state-sync.ts:2231-2239`) and `claimMirrorApply` one complete receipt
(`:2487-2498`). `state_sync` has `buildPagedModuleStateSyncPayloads`; claim mirror
has no equivalent, and the client exposes only replace and apply (`:2816-2825`).

Nothing bounds the total. The tool schema takes an unbounded content string
(`packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-memory/tools.ts:45-51`), the database only requires
non-empty content (`storage-claims-schema.ts:118-123`), and Rust mirror validation
has no content-size check (`crates/mc-store/src/claim_mirror.rs:303-367`). With
roughly 1 KiB of per-row overhead before content, the cap is reachable at a few
hundred ordinary claims, about fifty 20 KiB claims, or a single near-MiB claim.

Raising the cap to 32 MiB is mitigation, not a bound. The fix is a paged snapshot
seed with reassembly plus chunked atomic receipt delivery, so the payload size is
independent of the project's claim count.

`8ef978a6` aligned other claim wire limits but did not change these.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (module-state-sync.ts:2239).

title: Replace the cfg(test) legacy-memory gate with a runtime claim-lane decision
description:
`legacy_memory_compat` is a compile-time scaffold that leaves production with no
fallback when the claim lane is inactive.

```rust
fn legacy_memory_compat(ctx: &ProducerContext<'_>) -> bool {
    #[cfg(test)]
    { ctx.claim_lane.is_none() }
    #[cfg(not(test))]
    { let _ = ctx; false }
}
```
(`crates/mc-module/src/transform.rs:1931-1940`)

In release builds this is always `false`, so every caller takes the claim path.
`claim_snapshot_for_context` yields no claims when the lane is absent, disabled,
or its vector mismatches, and the legacy project-local read is unreachable. Tests
only compile the opposite branch, so the suite cannot observe this.

The reviewers' premise that the host omits `claim_lane` does not hold: the host
always assigns an object (`rust-mode-transform.ts:2312-2319`) with
`{enabled: claimLaneEnabled, snapshot_vector: ...}`. The reachable condition is
`enabled: false`, which is exactly what mirror suppression produces — and the
mirror-rebuild issue lists three ways to get there and stay there. The wire type
is `#[serde(default)] claim_lane: Option<ClaimLaneWire>`
(`transform.rs:900-929`), so an older or external host can still omit it.

Effect: project claim memory silently disappears from m0 for the whole epoch. The

title: Scope the claim mirror and its writes to an authorized route
description:
The committed claim mirror keeps one process-wide row set, but the host publishes
a route-specific authorized snapshot per session.

Mirror state is a singleton: `mc_claim_mirror_state` is declared
`id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1)` (`crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs:2727-2735`),
and every read and write targets `WHERE id = 1` or `VALUES (1, ...)`
(`crates/mc-store/src/claim_mirror.rs:654-687`, `777-836`, `893-900`). Projects,
claims, and receipts are additionally keyed by `database_incarnation_id`
(`lib.rs:2736-2782`), which does not permit two concurrent views because the
state row stays singleton and replacement clears every mirror table
(`claim_mirror.rs:709-714`).

One `McHandler` owns one store and all routes (`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:3010-3014`),
routes bind different project roots into it (`:12861-12874`), and the default
store path derives from the data home rather than the project root
(`:16883-16905`). Plugin storage is user-tier and shared across projects
(`packages/plugin/src/index.ts:106-108`).

So two sessions in different projects or workspaces, or with different
private-claim visibility, contend for the same rows. Session B starts with
`claimMirrorSeeded=false` (`rust-mode-transform.ts:807-845`) and calls
`claimMirrorReplace`; its snapshot differs from session A's, the comparison at
`claim_mirror.rs:793-810` fails, and with no `resetting` control row the result is
`ResetRequired` (`:813-815`). The host suppresses the error and disables the claim
lane for that session (`module-state-sync.ts:2414-2420`,
`rust-mode-transform.ts:2312-2319`).

Related, and best fixed together: `handle_claim_mirror_replace` and
`handle_claim_mirror_apply` (`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:10932-11010`) only check
that the route is bound. Neither maps the caller-supplied snapshot or receipt to
the bound `project_root`, so a bound route can write mirror state for a project it
does not own. `claim_route_root` exists (`:10743-10755`) but neither handler uses
it, and the store APIs receive no route information (`claim_mirror.rs:763-767`,
`869-874`). A test already demonstrates an arbitrary `projectId: 1` snapshot
succeeding on an unrelated bound route (`lib.rs:19659-19708`).

The caller here is the authenticated host plugin over an owner-only channel
(`connection-file.ts:69-75`, `auth.ts:227-277`), and mirror routes are not
model-facing tools, so this is a cross-route integrity gap rather than an
untrusted-agent hole. It still means a buggy or compromised host client can
corrupt another project's mirror.

`claim_route_root` alone is not sufficient for the authorization half: the wire
payload carries only local numeric project IDs, and one workspace can authorize
several projects. The fix needs either a server-side route-to-allowed-projects
grant or verifiable project identities on the wire, enforced in both handlers.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (mc-store/src/lib.rs:2728) and coderabbit
(mc-module/src/lib.rs:10980).

title: Give the claim mirror a reachable rebuild and reseed path
description:
Once the claim mirror and the host's snapshot disagree, nothing in the shipped
facade can bring them back into agreement, so the claim lane stays off for the
life of the install.

`replace_claim_mirror_snapshot` accepts a differing replacement only when the
mirror control state is `resetting` (`crates/mc-store/src/claim_mirror.rs:793-815`);
otherwise it returns `ResetRequired`. An exactly equivalent replacement succeeds
(`:807-811`), which is why the happy path works.

The host has no way to reach that state. `suppressClaimMirror` only sets
`claimMirrorSuppressed = true` (`module-state-sync.ts:2414-2420`).
`claimMirrorSeeded` is cleared only for `claim_mirror_not_seeded` (`:2522-2524`),
not for a generation mismatch or `ResetRequired`. No production caller reaches
`begin_claim_store_rebuild` — `rg` finds only its definition
(`crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs:15322`) and tests. `authority.prepare` is exposed
(`crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:13114-13116`) and does try to set `resetting`
(`lib.rs:15461-15467`), but that setter silently no-ops on the host's identity
format; see the separate store-identity issue.

Restart does not recover: a restarting host starts unseeded, rebuilds the same
differing snapshot, and gets `ResetRequired` again.

Three distinct triggers reach the divergence:

1. Workspace epoch changes with no claim receipt. Membership or sharing changes
   bump `project_memory_epoch` without producing a claim-operation receipt, so
   `pendingClaimMirrorReceipt` returns null while the vector moved. The branch at
   `module-state-sync.ts:2477-2483` throws and the catch suppresses the lane.

2. More than one receipt accumulates between passes. `vectorsAdvanceOneReceipt`
   (`:2267-2289`) requires exactly `+1` for each touched project, but the snapshot
   is captured once before the drain loop (`:2437-2441`, `:2470`) while the
   pending query selects only the first receipt (`:2247-2264`). Two receipts make
   the snapshot `+2`, so `claimMirrorGroup` throws at `:2332-2338`, no checkpoint
   advances, and the condition repeats. Sync runs per state-sync pass
   (`rust-mode-transform.ts:2279-2307`), not per tool call, so two parallel tool
   calls, another session, or background writes while this session is idle are
   enough.

3. A claim crosses `expiresAt` with no write. The provider omits it
   (`storage-claim-current-state.ts:361-368`), but expiry bumps no generation and
   writes no effect, so the vector still compares equal and the sync reports the
   mirror active. The stored row stays, and Rust does not filter expiry: the host
   puts `expiresAt` in generic attributes (`module-state-sync.ts:2144-2151`) while
   `MirroredClaimMemory` reads only lifecycle, category, importance, and content
   (`crates/mc-module/src/memory_render.rs:157-184`), and the transform loads every
   mirrored row (`crates/mc-module/src/transform.rs`). Expired claim content keeps
   being injected.

Wanted:

- A facade route that begins a claim-store rebuild, so the host can move the
  control state to `resetting` and then replace while frozen. This is the
  prerequisite for every recovery path below.
- Treat an epoch or project-set change with no pending receipt as a controlled
  full reseed rather than permanent suppression.
- When the pending backlog is not exactly one generation, either drain against
  per-receipt intermediate snapshots or reseed atomically.
- Filter `expiresAt` in Rust at selection time, and include visible-claim expiry
  in the rematerialization signal so a HARD pass reflects it.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (module-state-sync.ts:2482, :2491, :2485) and
coderabbit (module-state-sync.ts:2467).

title: Close five verified client and discovery findings from PR 32 review
description:
Five findings verified during the PR 32 review round but deliberately not fixed there, because each needs a behavior or shape decision rather than a mechanical edit. All are confirmed against code; none is speculative.

1. Control-request Cancel is structurally illegal. `cancel_key` emits `FrameId { channel: 0, epoch: 0, corr }` when an ambiguous control request (route.open) is cleaned up, but Section 6.2 requires Cancel on a current nonzero route and pending nonzero correlation, so the host closes the generation. Remedy is a choice: retire the generation locally (tears down every other route on the connection) or skip the Cancel and let the host request deadline settle it (leaves host-side work uncancelled for that window). Depends on how long an in-flight route.open can hold host resources.

2. The handshake deadline excludes discovery. `Client::connect` reads the connection file, then `connect_info` starts a fresh two-second deadline, so discovery is unbounded and dial plus authentication plus negotiation get the full budget again. Section 11.2 says the deadline spans discovery through negotiation. The snapshot is also blocking filesystem work on an async worker, so a stalled mount occupies the worker rather than merely overrunning. Fix moves the deadline before discovery and puts the snapshot in a bounded blocking task, which changes failure classification between handshake_timeout and discovery_failed.

3. `read_for_client` opens without `O_NONBLOCK`. A FIFO at the configured path blocks in `open` before `checked_stat` can reject it as non-regular, hanging `Client::connect` on a Tokio worker. The TypeScript reader already passes `O_NONBLOCK`, so the two discovery paths disagree. Adding the flag requires the subsequent bounded read to handle `EAGAIN`, or a hang becomes a truncated snapshot.

4. A late route open may survive client close. `close()` can drain the route set between the route.open response being delivered and `routes.insert(handle)`, after which `open_route` returns a handle that immediately fails `client_closed`, violating local-close-wins. A recheck must be atomic with the publish or it only moves the window; whether the close path then owes a route Goodbye depends on whether the handle was ever observable.

5. Replay reconnect may be unrecoverable at `max_connections` 1. `replay_frozen_once` appears to dial the replay connection while the old connection still holds its permit, so the host drops the new socket for capacity and `reconnect` fails before the cleanup that would free the permit. Releasing the old generation first has to preserve the frozen daemon id for the cross-incarnation comparison, so it is not a pure reorder.

Original review threads carry the full reasoning and the options considered for each.
acceptance_criteria: Each item either lands with a test that fails without it, or is closed with a recorded decision explaining why the current behavior is correct.
close_reason:
All five landed in acba0244, each with a test that fails without it.

Handshake deadline now starts before discovery, with the snapshot on the blocking pool under the shared budget. Connection file opens with O_NONBLOCK; the EAGAIN concern does not apply because checked_stat proves S_IFREG before any read. Control-request Cancel is no longer emitted at all, because a 0/0 identity has no legal frame and the host settles on its own deadline. Route handles publish under the lock close drains, with the closure recheck inside it; no route Goodbye is owed because close already sends the connection Goodbye. Replay reconnect releases the old generation first, which is safe because the frozen daemon id is a parameter rather than read off the old connection.

Two things the verification corrected. The FIFO test first passed for the wrong reason: open_parent requires an owner-only leaf parent, so a default-mode temp dir was rejected before open_file ran. With the dir chmodded to 0700 the un-fixed code hangs (timeout exit 124), confirming the block. The test now probes on a worker thread with a bounded join so the regression fails instead of wedging the suite.

Also learned while verifying: open_parent already does descriptor-relative per-component traversal with is_safe_ancestor on each, so the Rust reader does provide the ancestor safety the doc requires. The gap is TypeScript-only, as reported on that thread.

title: Expose kernel disposition events through daemon commands
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` (R1, R3, R5, R7).

## Goal
Provide a production daemon route and explicit host command flow for rejected, quarantined, disputed, and explicitly stale dispositions.

## Scope
- Accept target object, disposition kind, actor, cause, evidence references, and idempotency key.
- Validate endpoint type and permitted transition in the daemon.
- Represent rejection and quarantine as staging admission decisions.
- Represent dispute and explicit staleness as append-only canonical lifecycle or eligibility events, not proposition truth fields.
- Commit the disposition event, change-event entry, affected admission state, and outbox rows in one transaction.
- Wire thin clients through normal user confirmation. Clients do not write disposition state directly.
design: The daemon maps each disposition to an admission decision or canonical lifecycle event, writes the commit envelope, and returns committed commit_seq and resulting eligibility.
acceptance_criteria: Every supported disposition is available through daemon route and explicit host command; visibility-changing actions require confirmation; staging dispositions stay invisible; canonical dispositions atomically affect injection eligibility; duplicate submissions are idempotent; invalid transitions make no partial writes; restart preserves state.
notes: No authority-convergence channel or client-side mirror is retained.

title: MODULE-authority native rendering needs a claim-policy decision channel
description:
Under MODULE memory authority, the native render path (mc-store load_active_memories and the m1 lane) selects active/permanent unexpired rows with no claim-policy or verification predicate, and the TypeScript state-sync policy filter never applies because memory sections are omitted while the module owns the lane (module-state-sync.ts omitAuthorityMemorySections). A /ctx_memory write under MODULE authority therefore creates an active, unverified native row that the next native transform injects automatically — a CANDIDATE bypasses the v86 visibility ladder entirely in rust mode.

Raised by codex review on PR #24 (inline comment 3840295420). Deferred from the PR because the fix needs an authority-model design decision, not a mechanical patch: while MODULE owns the lane, TypeScript (the policy authority) has no channel to push per-row eligibility without violating the one-writer-per-pool rule that fences the memories section (mc-store apply gates PREPARING/MODULE/DRAINING).

Candidate shapes to evaluate:
1. A dedicated policy sidecar section in state_sync (eligibility verdicts keyed by native row id) that the apply lane accepts even under MODULE authority, since it carries no row content — keeps Rust free of policy derivation.
2. Mirror auto_eligible into mc_memories via the module-to-TS changefeed round trip: TS adjudicates module-created rows on the reverse sync and pushes the verdict back; native render gains a WHERE auto_eligible = 1 predicate. Requires a default for not-yet-adjudicated rows (fail closed = candidate-invisible until adjudicated; fail open = today's behavior).
3. Derive a conservative native predicate from existing columns (verification_status) — rejected on first pass: USER_EXPLICIT-taint rows are auto-eligible without verification, so this under-renders legitimate content.

Acceptance: under MODULE authority, a freshly written unverified memory does not render into the native m0/m1 lanes until the policy authority marks it eligible; explicit get keeps working with trust labels; no policy derivation logic moves into Rust.

## Context
PR #24 v86 claim trust policy follow-up
close_reason: Obsolete: the TS-policy-to-module push channel is unnecessary under one daemon authority.

The decision channel must either keep policy revocations crossing the boundary in authority mode (e.g. send the delete lane even when snapshot sections are omitted) or move the policy evaluator natively.
