title: Incident verifier validation cannot resolve the shm-hardening-u1 cargo verifier
description:
## Problem

`Incident regression pool (supported TS)` fails at its first step, "Reject
changed mutation-bound verifiers without replay evidence":

    bun run --cwd packages/e2e-tests validate:incident-verifiers
    mutations/shm-hardening-u1.json.mutations[0]: cannot resolve a verifier from
    command "cargo test -p mc-shm-transport --test iceoryx
    allocation_slack_never_reaches_the_frame_decoder"

The validator cannot map that cargo invocation to a known verifier, so the gate
rejects the mutation as unverifiable.

## Not caused by PR 78

Reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree with the identical message, so this
is latent on main. The job is path-gated and was SKIPPED on main's own recent CI
runs, which is why it surfaced first on a PR.

    git worktree add --detach /tmp/main-check origin/main
    cd /tmp/main-check && bun run --cwd packages/e2e-tests validate:incident-verifiers

Nothing in the failing path touches anti-memory; it is the SHM transport
hardening mutation.

## Likely shape

Either the validator's command-to-verifier resolution does not understand
`--test <target> <filter>` for a cargo test, or the named test moved or was
renamed and the mutation record still points at the old invocation. Both are
cheap to confirm by grepping for
`allocation_slack_never_reaches_the_frame_decoder` in `crates/mc-shm-transport`.

## Acceptance

- `validate:incident-verifiers` passes on main.
- If the resolver was the gap, it has a test covering the cargo `--test target
  filter` form so the next mutation of that shape does not silently fail the gate.

title: Anti-memory payload fields have no write-side length ceiling
description:
## Problem

`requiredText` normalizes whitespace and rejects empty values but imposes no
length limit (`memory/storage-anti-memory.ts`), and no content-length bound was
found anywhere on the claim write path. A single `ctx_memory` call can therefore
store a payload field of arbitrary size, and `renderAntiMemoryContent`
concatenates up to ten of them into the claim content.

Three consumers have each been bitten by this and each now bounds it locally:

1. `searchAntiMemories` caps the assembled passage at
   `ANTI_MEMORY_MAX_PASSAGE_BYTES` before the token scan and the embedding batch
   (d8590591).
2. `partitionVerifyScope` excludes a record whose content exceeds
   `MAX_VERIFY_CLAIM_CONTENT_BYTES` from the verification batch, because
   `buildVerifyPrompt` interpolates content whole for up to `VERIFY_BATCH_SIZE`
   records and one outsized record failed the entire batch repeatedly.
3. The renderers truncate each field at `MAX_RENDER_FIELD_BYTES`.

Both reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #78.

Three independent consumers bounding the same unbounded field is the signal that
the bound belongs at the write. The local caps are containment, not the fix.

## Consequence of leaving it

An oversized record is currently stored, rendered truncated, matched truncated,
and never verified — so it can never reach VERIFIED maturity and never appears on
an automatic surface. It is silently inert rather than broken, which is worse
than a rejection at write time.

## Decision needed

A per-field ceiling in `requiredText` / `optionalText` is one edit, but it is a
storage-contract change with an agent-visible error surface: `ctx_memory` create
and the verification UPDATE path would start failing on an over-long field
instead of accepting it. That needs a deliberate choice between rejecting and
truncating at write, and a decision about pre-existing rows.

## Acceptance

- A per-field length ceiling is enforced at the write boundary, with the
  rejection or truncation behaviour tested on both the `ctx_memory` create path
  and `parseAntiMemoryContent`.
- The verification-gate exclusion keeps covering pre-existing oversized rows, or
  a migration retires them.

title: Anti-memory lane caps candidates by claim recency before any relevance test
description:
## Problem

`searchAntiMemories` selects its candidate set with
`listActiveAntiMemoryPublicIds`, which orders by `claim_id DESC` and applies
`LIMIT MAX_LANE_CANDIDATES` (150):

    packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-anti-memory.ts:546-570

Recency is the only selector. Query matching happens afterwards, in memory. Once
a project holds more than 150 active anti-memories, an older warning that
exactly matches the requested strategy is unreachable by both explicit and
automatic search — not ranked low, absent from the candidate set.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #78 (P2).

The workspace half of that report is fixed in b4f6908e: the listing now reads
`ownProjectIds` rather than the expanded workspace set, because anti-memory
records are written `sharing: "private"` and a co-member's warning can never
clear the authorization step — it could only consume the ceiling and then be
dropped, hiding the caller's own warnings behind claims they cannot see.

The recency-before-relevance half remains and needs an index.

## Why it is not a review fix

Selecting relevant candidates before the ceiling requires a lexical index over
anti-memory payload text. Today the lane tokenizes payload values in TypeScript
after hydration, so there is nothing to query. That is the same gap the
claims-native lexical index work covers, and it should land with it rather than
as a bespoke index for one lane.

## Acceptance

- Candidate selection for the anti-memory lane is driven by query match, with
  recency as a tiebreak rather than the selector.
- A test seeds more than `MAX_LANE_CANDIDATES` active anti-memories, then finds
  the oldest one by an exact match on its rejected strategy.

title: Check (plugin) is flaky under 8-way shard parallelism
description:
`Check (plugin)` has load-sensitive tests that fail intermittently on CI and pass
locally, under the 8-way shard parallelism in `scripts/test-shard.sh`
(`xargs -P "$n"`, n = nproc capped at 8).

Two of the four observed cases were file-identity tests and are FIXED on PR #77
(`reset marker and interrupted quarantine`, `doctor reset-db scenario 5b`): both
deleted a file and recreated it, and CI recycled the freed inode so a
"replacement" kept its recorded dev+inode. Both now stage a sibling and rename it
into place. Remaining below.

## AE1: two-process bootstrap loses to SQLITE_BUSY

`storage-db direct format > ... two processes bootstrap one pristine family
#then both converge on one incarnation (AE1)`
(`storage-db.test.ts:227`). Failed on PR #77 run 33142755979 and independently on
main job 98678677487, so it is not branch-specific.

It is not an assertion drift. One spawned worker exits 1 with:

    [magic-context] storage unavailable: database is locked.
      at openDatabase (storage-db.ts:860)
      at bootstrap-worker.ts:2

so `expect(exitCode).toBe(0)` sees 1. Two workers race to bootstrap the same
pristine family; under shard contention one exceeds SQLite's busy timeout.

Worth deciding whether this is only a test-environment issue or whether
`openDatabase` should tolerate a concurrent bootstrap rather than surfacing
SQLITE_BUSY as fatal — the test name asserts both processes converge, which is a
production claim about concurrent first-open.

## Embedding corpus cap: 5s default timeout

`embedding measurement corpus > bounds a session's corpus rows, keeping the
newest when the cap is exceeded` at 5010.94ms against bun's 5000ms default.
Inserts `MEASUREMENT_CORPUS_SESSION_ROW_CAP + 5` = 2005 rows one at a time, and
`recordEmbeddingMeasurement` is a bare `INSERT OR IGNORE` plus a cap trim with no
transaction of its own, so the loop pays ~2005 auto-commit transactions.

Cheapest fix: wrap the loop in one `db.transaction(...)` in the test. The cap
logic still runs per insert, so the assertion is unchanged.

## Evidence that it is flakiness, not a deterministic failure

Three runs of the same commit produced three DIFFERENT failures: embedding corpus,
then AE1, then doctor-reset-db scenario 5b.

title: Refresh anti-memory expiry when dedup attaches a repeated correction
description:
Found in review of PR #77 (stack/anti-memory-03-writers), confirmed against the
code. Not fixed there: the correct fix changes the create-stage contract, so it
wants its own change and its own tests.

## Behavior

`stageCreateAntiMemoryInCurrentTransaction` passes an event-anchored
`expiresAt` (event.createdAt + ANTI_MEMORY_DEFAULT_TTL_MS) into
`stageCreateProjectMemoryClaimInCurrentTransaction`. When the same rejected
strategy is observed again and normalizes onto an existing live
(project, category, normalized_hash) slot, that function takes the dedup branch
and calls `attachEvidenceStage`, which inserts a `claim_evidence` row and
nothing else. The requested `expiresAt` is dropped.

Result: an anti-memory expires 90 days after the FIRST correction even when an
identical correction recurred recently, so a still-live rejected approach stops
warning while it is still being repeated.

## Why it is not a small patch

`claim_memory_revision_attributes` is strictly append-only — there are
BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers that RAISE(ABORT). Expiry lives in that
per-revision row, so extending a TTL means appending a revision, not updating a
column.

Appending a revision from inside the create stage needs, at minimum:

- a mutation token for the existing claim, mintable via
  `computeProjectMemoryMutationToken`
- a revision append via `stageReviseProjectMemoryClaimInCurrentTransaction`,
  which also has to carry `antiMemoryWriter: true` past the staging-boundary
  guard
- a typed payload row (`insertPayload`) for the NEW revision, or
  `readAntiMemory` throws `ClaimGraphCorruptionError`
- merging two stage outcomes into the single `ClaimOperationStageOutcome` the
  caller expects: effects, `policyRevisionIds`, and
  `mutationTokenPublicClaimIds`, keeping effect keys distinct so the
  UNIQUE (receipt_id, effect_key) append-only constraint still holds

## Acceptance

- A repeated correction whose event-anchored expiry is later than the stored one
  extends the existing anti-memory instead of only attaching evidence.
- A repeated correction whose expiry is NOT later leaves expiry unchanged and
  still attaches evidence (no pointless revision, and replay stays idempotent).
- Harvest remains idempotent under replay: re-running the same event produces the
  receipt replay path, not a second revision.

title: replace_profile reports an uncommitted failure after the rename already committed
description:
`GenerationStore::replace_profile` renames the new `current-profile.json` into
place and then fsyncs the lifecycle root:

    renameat(root_fd, temp, root_fd, CURRENT_PROFILE_NAME)?;
    fsync_preserving_storage(&root_fd, "lifecycle root fsync failed")?;

If the fsync fails, the rename has already taken effect — the namespace contains
the new selector — but the call returns an error whose documented contract says
`current` is unchanged and no other generation was selected. Callers therefore
report that promotion failed while a subsequent production resolution observes
the newly selected digest, and a `restart` can leave the incumbent stopped on the
strength of a promotion that actually happened.

This is an unknown-outcome gap rather than a missing check, and it needs a
contract decision:

- `GenerationError`'s variants are documented as mapping onto exactly one closed
  v1 reason each, and none of the contract's `cli.reasons.failing_by_precedence`
  entries expresses "committed, durability unproven".
- Rolling the selector back is itself fallible and would need its own
  unknown-outcome answer, so it moves the problem rather than solving it.
- Returning success would hide a real durability loss.

Whatever shape is chosen has to be reflected in the closed reason set and in
`generation_failure`'s mapping, so it is not a review-pass edit.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #49 (comment 3875686012).

title: macOS build of mc-host is broken: RawMode is u16, generation.rs passes u32
description:
The `Shared memory source build (macos-latest)` CI job fails to compile
`mc-host` on macOS with three `E0308` errors in
`crates/mc-host/src/generation.rs`:

    835:9  expected `u32`, found `u16`   (ManifestFile { mode, .. })
    851:29 expected `u16`, found `u32`   (Mode::from_raw_mode(mode))
    857:49 expected `u16`, found `u32`   (Mode::from_raw_mode(mode))

`rustix::fs::RawMode` is `u16` on Apple targets and `u32` on Linux, so the
`mode: u32` locals in `copy_source_into` and `write_new_file` do not line up.
`Mode::from_raw_mode(0o700)`-style literal calls are fine because the literal
infers to `RawMode`; only the named `u32` bindings break.

Pre-existing: reproduced on run 32993522924 against commit 2cd8a484, before the
PR #49 review work. The fix is likely a `RawMode`-typed alias or `.into()` at
those three sites, but it needs an actual macOS build to confirm rather than a
reasoned patch, and the same job should then be re-checked for further mismatches
behind these three.

Relevant context for the deferred macOS lane: this means `mc-host` does not
currently build on Darwin at all, which is a bigger gap than the missing
`/dev/fd` exec path in `spawn.rs` (`libc::fexecve` and
`libc::SYS_close_range` are Linux-only, so the launcher cannot build there
either). Both were raised on PR #49 by chatgpt-codex-connector, on the premise
that `release/mc-host-release.json` advertises `darwin-arm64` and
`darwin-x64` as supported platforms.

title: Stage payload sources through a pinned root descriptor
description:
`copy_source_into` opens each staging source by full pathname:

    openat(CWD, &*spec.source, RDONLY | NOFOLLOW | CLOEXEC | NONBLOCK, ...)

`O_NOFOLLOW` constrains only the final component, so an intermediate component
of the payload directory that is replaced with a symlink after
`payload_sources` enumerated the tree and before staging opens the file is
followed. The before/after `fstat` identity checks then compare the substituted
object with itself and agree, so the generation is promoted with bytes that were
never under the requested payload tree.

Why this is not a contained fix: `SourceSpec.source` is an absolute path and the
public API deliberately allows staging from an arbitrary location — a hard link
into a package cache is called out as acceptable, and the source path is not
required to match `rel_path` (the tests rely on that). Closing the hole means
changing the staging contract, roughly one of:

- have `payload_sources` return retained descriptors instead of paths, and
  `stage_and_promote` consume descriptors;
- add a pinned payload-root descriptor plus root-relative source paths, and
  resolve each source with the existing `open_rel_nofollow` walk.

The second keeps `SourceSpec` closer to its current shape but only fits callers
whose sources share one root, which the dev walk does and the tests do not.

Scope note: the exposed flow is `--payload-dir`, the dev and test staging path.
Production resolution is read-only and U9 records
`production_qualified:false`, so no supported flow stages a production payload
today. The attacker must already be able to write inside the directory the user
pointed the flag at.

title: status should report incompatible_daemon once U3 lands authenticated version propagation
description:
`cmd_probe` classifies every coherent `Running` observation as `healthy`, so
monitoring and upgrade tooling see an incumbent daemon outside this release's
supported range as healthy — while `start` rejects the same publication value
through `daemon_version_compatible` and returns `incompatible_daemon`.

The asymmetry is deliberate today, not an oversight. `publication_daemon_ver`
is documented as untrusted:

    Untrusted publication diagnostics (daemon_ver) for the versions block.
    Authenticated version propagation is U3's client work; until then the
    discovery-validated publication value is reported as a diagnostic only.

`start` uses the value only after an authenticated connect. `status` dials no
connection at all — that is its contract — so basing an `ok:false` verdict on
the value would elevate an unauthenticated self-declaration into an
authoritative health verdict.

Once U3 lands authenticated version propagation, `status` should apply the
range check and return the contract's `incompatible_daemon` result.

Interim mitigation for tooling: `status` already emits the observed value in
`versions.daemon`, and `ck-mc-host release-info` exposes
`versions.supported_daemon_range`, so a caller that needs the comparison today
can make it from one `status` invocation without a second round trip.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #49 (comment 3875496780).

title: Decide the launcher executable trust predicate against the supported install layouts
description:
`spawn.rs`'s `spawn_detached` validates the retained `/proc/self/exe`
descriptor as a regular file owned by the invoking UID, and now also rejects an
other-writable inode. Two adjacent questions are unresolved, and both hinge on
what modes and owners the contract's four `install_layouts`
(`bun_physical_link`, `compiled_bun_external`, `npm_hoisted`, `npm_nested`)
actually produce in practice.

1. Group-writable executables are still accepted. On a host with a shared
   primary group that is a real exposure: another group member can rewrite the
   inode and `fexecve` runs their bytes as this user. But a umask of 002 —
   the default on several distributions with user-private groups — leaves
   npm-installed files at 0775, where "group" is the user alone. Rejecting
   group-writable would fail those installs closed with `internal_error` and
   remediation `report_bug`, which is the wrong answer for a routine umask.

2. Root-owned executables are rejected. `scripts/install.sh` runs
   `npx -y "$PACKAGE@latest" setup` with no `-g`, `--prefix`, or `sudo`,
   so the supported path yields a user-owned launcher and the rejection is
   unreachable today. If a system-wide layout is ever supported, the predicate
   should accept root-owned-and-not-group/other-writable, which is the rule
   `instance::is_safe_ancestor` already applies to directories.

Both should be settled together, with the accepted ownership and mode set moving
alongside whatever the `install.layout` contract check declares supported —
rather than guessed at from either direction.

Note this becomes less pressing once U6/U9 qualify real payloads: the
`ponytail:` note at the top of `spawn.rs` says the retained fd becomes
`ValidatedGeneration::open_verified_file("bin/ck-mc-host")`, and the
generation store already enforces `st_uid == owner_uid()` and owner-only modes
on every staged file, so the long-term path is owner-only by construction.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #49 (comments 3875296522 and
3875496786).

title: restart preflight must prove staging capacity before committing the stop
description:
`restart --payload-dir` can commit an irreversible stop and then fail with
`insufficient_storage` and no successor, even though the shortfall was
observable on disk beforehand.

`preflight_generation` only enumerates the payload sources for the dev
staging path (`payload_sources(dir)`). The capacity check lives in
`GenerationStore::stage_and_promote`, which runs inside `start_phase` after
`stop_phase` has already taken the serving daemon down. The result is
`stop_committed:true`, `start_committed:false` — the exact outage class
`preflight_generation`'s own doc comment says it exists to prevent.

Why this is not a one-line preflight: `resolve_generation` prunes
unreferenced generations and stale temps *before* staging, so space that is
unavailable at preflight time may be freed by the prune that runs after the
stop. Comparing `required_stage_bytes(sources)` against
`available_bytes()` in the preflight would therefore refuse restarts that
would have succeeded, trading one outage class for another.

A sound preflight needs a read-only "bytes reclaimable by prune" measurement
on GenerationStore so the check can be `required <= available + prunable`.
That is a new store API plus boundary tests, not a review-comment-sized edit.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #49 (comment 3873334021,
crates/mc-module/src/bin/ck-mc-host.rs:639). Declined there with this
rationale.

title: Claim-mirror follow-ups: source attribution, consumer seeding, cross-project receipts
description:
Smaller claim-mirror gaps found in PR #38 review that are real but not blocking,
grouped because each is a few lines in one or two files.

1. Foreign-workspace source attribution is dropped in the mirror.
   `claimMirrorRow` stores `provenanceLabel: item.explicitLabel`
   (`packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-state-sync.ts:2133-2158`).
   Auto-injection items carry `explicitLabel: null`
   (`storage-claim-current-state.ts:300-330`, `:388-392`), so the field is
   effectively always empty. The TypeScript path derives a foreign source display
   name from project identity instead (`inject-compartments.ts:1036-1049`,
   `workspaces.ts:254-267`) and renders it as `[source]`
   (`claim-memory-render.ts:77-82`). Rust renders `provenance_label` as the
   bracketed label (`crates/mc-module/src/memory_render.rs:207-223`), so a foreign
   project's fact appears indistinguishable from the current project's own facts in
   native transforms. Fix: populate the mirror's `provenanceLabel` from the foreign
   project display name, which needs `namesByIdentity` and
   `canonicalIdentityByStoredPath` threaded through `ModuleWorkspaceContext`.
   Separately, the historian ignores `provenance_label` entirely
   (`historian_prompt.rs:327-350`), so historian claim blocks carry no source
   attribution at all.

2. A fresh claim-effect consumer still walks its projects' whole history.
   Scoping the prefix query to the target mutation's projects is done, but a
   long-lived install can hold more than the 1,000-group cap within one project, so
   the first module-owned mutation in that project can still fail after its write
   committed. Fix: seed a new consumer checkpoint at the target project's
   predecessors instead of starting from zero.
   (`module-state-sync.ts` `drainClaimEffectPrefix`.)

3. Cross-workspace relocation receipts cannot be projected.
   `claimMirrorGroup` rejects a receipt whose `touchedProjects` includes a project
   outside the snapshot's vector (`module-state-sync.ts:2332-2338`). A move emits
   effects for both source and target in one receipt
   (`relocate-memory.ts:254-350`), and relocation requires only that the target
   resolves and differs from the source (`:167-215`) — no shared-workspace check.
   Not currently reachable: `rg` finds no production caller of
   `moveProjectMemoryClaims` or `copyProjectMemoryClaims`. Before wiring relocation
   up, either require same-workspace relocation or add per-authorized-project
   receipt projections.

4. `validate_claim` canonically encodes `attributes`, `applicability`, and `policy`
   and discards the result, then `insert_claim` re-encodes the same three fields to
   build its SQL parameters (`crates/mc-store/src/claim_mirror.rs`, validation
   around `:355`, insert around `:583-586`). Double the JSON encoding per claim per
   snapshot or receipt. Left alone deliberately: threading the encoded strings from
   validation into insert is a real signature change for an unmeasured win, so it
   wants a measurement first.

Reported on PR #38 by codex (module-state-sync.ts:2157, :2338, :2708) and claude
(claim_mirror.rs:355).

title: Give outgoing-frame byte accounting one owner in wire.rs
description:
Two byte-accounting implementations coexist in mc-host, and two reservation orderings.

`client.rs` defines a mutex-backed `ByteCounter`/`ByteCharge` whose `charge(usize) -> Option<ByteCharge>` is contract-for-contract what `wire::ByteBudget::try_charge(usize) -> Option<wire::ByteCharge>` already provides: synchronous, non-blocking, all-or-none, RAII release on drop. The wire version additionally has `split`, `shrink_to`, `capacity`, `available`, and its own tests. Both crates also name their charge type `ByteCharge`, so the two are distinguishable only by module path.

Feasibility checked: `CLIENT_QUEUED_BYTES` is 65 MiB, far below the semaphore permit ceiling `try_charge` converts against, so the swap is mechanical. Call sites: `Inner.queue_budget`, `Inner.retained_budget`, `encode_data_frame`, the `dispatch` retained-charge path, `admit`, `ChargedItem._charge`, and the tests that read `ByteCounter::used()` (which becomes `available()`).

Separately, the two reservation orderings disagree. `connection.rs::reserve_catalog_frame` charges before encoding, computing frame size by hand as `body.len() + HEADER_LEN`. `client.rs::encode_data_frame` encodes first and charges the encoded length afterward, so the encoded buffer is briefly unaccounted. Both are locally correct; neither is the single rule, and a future change to reservation semantics has to find both.

Scope: move the client onto `wire::ByteBudget`, then decide one ordering and express it as a shared helper in `wire.rs` so header accounting cannot drift between call sites. Deliberately not folded into a review round on an already-large change: it touches live accounting on the client hot path and deserves its own diff.
acceptance_criteria: One byte-accounting type backs both paths; frame reservation goes through one helper; existing budget tests still pass.

title: Dreamer: persist the attempt harness for in-flight classify commands
description:
A dreamer.run_task handler cancelled after Broca accepted a run but before the response was ledgered leaves the Broca run alive by design. A retry of the same durable command through a different harness binding derives the same child-session string but opens it under a different (project_root, harness, session) key, so Broca's byte-identical send dedup does not match and a second billable run starts while the original may still be executing.

The in-process command guard closes this for a single live host, and the historian path is now covered because its awaiting state persists producer_harness. Classify has no equivalent durable in-flight state: mc_dream_task_commands records only the final response, so there is nowhere to record the attempt harness today.

Closing it needs a durable in-flight record written before the first attempt and cleared or superseded on completion, which adds a write to the classify hot path and a crash-cleanup story for rows whose host died mid-attempt. That is a design change rather than a fix, so it is deliberately not folded into the Broca runner-route work.

Raised in review of PR 28 (comment 3844564006).

title: Extract a shared two-step confirmation helper for claim commands and ctx-recomp
description: PR #24 round-45 (comment 3843922483): runConfirmedClaimMutation (claim-policy-commands.ts) and packages/pi-plugin/src/commands/ctx-recomp.ts each hand-roll a Map<sessionKey,{timestamp,argsKey}> + 60s window + argsKey-equality confirmation. Eviction differs (ctx-recomp evicts on !warning.confirmable; claim commands sweep stale entries per call). Extract one PendingConfirmation helper in core that both import, preserving each caller's eviction semantics explicitly, so window/eviction/key-scheme changes land in one place.

title: Host: derive the resident-byte ceiling from declarations instead of a Broca-shaped default
description:
HostLimits::default() currently computes max_resident_bytes as 256 MiB plus broca::config::DECLARED_RETAINED_RESIDENT_BYTES, so a generic default reaches into one component's constants and every deployment that never composes Broca still inherits Broca-shaped sizing.

The knob's meaning is what forces this: max_resident_bytes is an absolute total ceiling, and the runtime subtracts each component's declared retained reservation from it to derive ingress headroom. A generic default therefore cannot be correct without knowing which components will be composed.

The fix is to change what the operator configures: let max_resident_bytes express ingress headroom and have the runtime add the composed handler's resource_declarations() to it, which runtime.rs already sums as reservations.retained_bytes for its resident-floor validation. That removes the hardcoded default entirely rather than relocating the coupling.

This is deferred because it changes the meaning of an operator-visible knob and touches every configuration and test that sets it, which does not belong in the Broca runner-route change.

title: Historian: durable ambiguous-send phase before refire
description: PR 28 review follow-up (codex comment 3841661859): when both the original session.send and its one recovery resend are accepted by Broca but both responses are lost (two consecutive connection failures), the historian abandons the firing to Idle with no run id; the next firing increments firing_seq and starts a second billable run while the first may still be active under the old producer session. Fix shape: a durable 'send accepted, outcome unknown, session X' phase so a later pass reattaches to or purges that exact session before authorizing a refire. A best-effort purge on the abandon path cannot work because the connection that would carry it is the one that just failed. Consequence today is bounded wasted spend (orphaned run capped by Broca's run allowance; firing-seq fence keeps its output out of the store), not corrupted state.

title: Flaky host-behavior E2E: historian/emergency timing tests fail intermittently in CI
description: Observed on PR 28 (feat/broca-runner-route): 'B12 project epoch bump HARD-refolds', 'pi short context accumulating overflow > emergency bypass ... slow historian', and 'emergency >=95% > historian is invoked when usage crosses 95%' each failed in DIFFERENT CI runs of the same commit range and pass locally at the same commit. Timing/usage-threshold sensitivity under CI load. Also: scripts/test-shard.sh masks per-shard failures behind xargs exit 123 while printing only the last shard's '0 fail' summary, which hides real failures locally -- worth surfacing an aggregated shard summary.

title: e2e harness: historian subprocess bypasses the mock provider on hosts with real credentials
description: Discovered during PR#24 CI triage: on a developer host where opencode has real provider credentials, the plugin's historian request does not reach the e2e mock provider (h.mock.requests() shows 0 historian matches) and instead produces non-deterministic real-model compartments (observed two different titles across identical runs: 'Filler turns with repeated keyword-soup text, no substantive work' / 'Filler turns of repeated keyword text, no substantive work'). On GitHub runners the same tests route historian traffic to the mock correctly. Effect: historian e2e tests can pass locally for the wrong reason and hide mock-payload bugs (emergency-blocking.test.ts hid an invalid empty historian payload this way — fixed separately by returning a valid v2 tiered payload). Fix direction: make the spawned opencode/plugin historian subprocess inherit the harness provider override (or strip real credentials in the child env) so local runs are as hermetic as CI.

title: Kernel origin guard requires asserted supporting evidence
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` (R1, R3, R4, R7).

## Goal
Prevent an admission or enforcement policy record from naming evidence as its origin unless that evidence has an asserted supporting relation to the governed object.

## Scope
- Validate origin references during daemon commit processing.
- Require an effective asserted `supports` edge whose endpoint kinds satisfy the relation registry.
- Do not treat `merged_from`, identity, provenance-only, or inferred relations as support.
- Allow an edge created in the same transaction to satisfy validation.
- Preserve merge and adoption operations that do not claim unsupported evidence as policy origin.
design: Commit validation resolves the proposed origin against asserted edges visible in the transaction before finalizing the commit envelope.
acceptance_criteria: An asserted supports edge permits a valid origin; merged_from or inferred support does not; wrong endpoint kinds and cross-domain references fail; same-transaction support commits atomically; failed validation writes no partial canonical state or outbox rows.
notes: This guard enforces evidence provenance; it does not implement the deferred policy-set evaluator.

title: module sync: mid-session compatibility events from held-open v85 writers bypass snapshot watermarks
description: Codex PR#24 comment 3839789384. A held-open v85 process appending stale/flagged verification events mid-session cannot bump project_memory_epoch, so cached automatic lanes (module mirror via module-state-sync watermarks, m0 recheck keyed on epoch/workspace-fingerprint in inject-compartments) keep serving the soft-hidden row until restart or an unrelated hard fold. Startup is now covered: reconcileCompatibilityVerificationsAtStartup bumps affected project epochs for unexamined negative events (d3d83eb5 follow-up commit). Residual: mid-session events need a compatibility-event watermark component in ModuleWatermarks + the m0 recheck state, or a periodic reconcile tick. Watermark shape change touches acked_watermarks round-trip; verify mc-module tolerates additive fields.
close_reason: Obsolete: this v85-writer compatibility machinery is removed because incompatible memory databases are discarded.

title: claims seeding: pre-v86 model rewrites can carry inherited explicit_user observations
description: Codex PR#24 comment 3839697932: before liveRewriteSourceType() landed, the rewrite path passed the retained row.source_type into createMemoryObservation, so a model rewrite of a user-sourced memory minted a supports observation with source_trust_class=explicit_user. hasExplicitUserEvidence counts any such observation (the seed-boundary guard only covers the retained-metadata path), so v86 seeding can promote an arbitrary pre-v86 replacement to VERIFIED. No recorded discriminator separates those observations from genuine user attestations (same producer, same source_type, same trust class; an observation-id watermark cannot distinguish held-open v85 writes from genuine post-boundary user creations). Fixing requires a design decision about which historical observation lineages count as user attestation (e.g. only claim-origin observations, or an extractor/producer allowlist) with an assessment of how much legit corpus each choice demotes.
close_reason: Resolved in PR#24 commit 172ead5a: hasExplicitUserEvidence restricts both evidence branches (explicit_user observations and retained user metadata) to the claim's FIRST revision when the revision is at or below the seed boundary. This is the 'origin-revision-only' option: it mirrors the live build's rule that every rewrite is model_inference (liveRewriteSourceType returns null unconditionally, user-driven or not), applied retroactively. Corpus impact: pre-v86 rewrite revisions of user memories seed as CANDIDATE instead of VERIFIED and re-enter via verification or /ctx-approve — the PR's fail-closed posture. Regression test: 'pre-boundary rewrite revisions cannot inherit explicit-user trust' in storage-claim-policy.test.ts.

title: module authority: policy visibility must reach the native m0/ctx_search lane
description: Codex PR#24 comment 3839697928: while memory authority is MODULE, module-state-sync omits the memories/memory_mutations sections (one-writer rule, omitAuthorityMemorySections), so TypeScript claim-policy transitions (quarantine, rejection, contradiction, CANDIDATE demotion) never reach the native store, and Rust serves m0/ctx_search from unfiltered native rows. The ctx_memory tool lane is gated TS-side (id translation + write preflight), but the native injection/search lane is not. Needs a policy-visibility channel that does not violate the one-writer rule — e.g. an eligibility id-set / prune list pushed alongside the authority mirror, or policy evaluation before rows enter the native store. Wire protocol + mc-module/mc-store work.
close_reason: duplicate of magic-context-658 (same MODULE-authority policy-visibility gap, earlier Codex round)

title: module sync: prune policy-hidden foreign workspace rows from the native mirror
description: CodeRabbit PR#24 comment 3839673875: when a foreign workspace member's memory flips policy-ineligible, this session's workspace snapshot omits the row but the replace scope deliberately names only ownIdentities (module-state-sync.ts memoriesReplaceProjects), so the already-mirrored foreign row survives in the native store until the foreign project's own next sync prunes it. Design a bounded removal for omitted foreign projection rows without declaring the share-filtered snapshot authoritative for the whole foreign project (per-row tombstones or a share-scoped prune set); needs wire-protocol + mc-module/mc-store changes and a test for a foreign policy transition removing a previously mirrored shared row.
close_reason: Obsolete: the native memory mirror is deleted by the kernel architecture.

title: Measure and remove duplicate Synapse tokenization safely
description:
## Context

`Backend::embed` performs a sequential tokenizer validation pass over every input, then calls FastEmbed, which tokenizes the same batch again. Large-text microbench evidence found the first pass can be material, but deleting it naively changes error classification and can condemn the entire Synapse lane for one bad input. This task measures the production path, then removes the duplicate pass only if a semantics-preserving design earns the change.

This work was split from `magic-context-18r`. The hash and depth-scanner edits are local and independently verifiable; tokenization depends on the real model bundle, FastEmbed behavior, failure taxonomy, and peak-memory evidence.

## Verified current state

- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs` `Backend::embed` locks `TextEmbedding`, loops over `texts`, rejects empty text, and calls `model.tokenizer.encode(text, true)` to reject tokenization failure or zero-token output.
- The same function then calls `model.embed(texts, None)`. FastEmbed performs its own batch tokenization before ORT inference.
- The pre-pass is load-bearing today. It maps bad input to `InferenceError::Input`. Without it, FastEmbed tokenization failures currently enter the generic `InferenceError::Invariant` path.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs` `settle_inference` marks the lane failing on invariant errors. One malformed or zero-token input must not disable a healthy model lane.
- Whitespace-only text can pass the non-empty string boundary. The committed tiny tokenizer has no post-processor and can produce zero IDs, which would make mean pooling invalid.
- Replacing the loop with one retained `encode_batch` result is not automatically better. Holding all encodings can convert a bounded per-item temporary into batch-sized uncharged memory.
- `magic-context-c50.8` owns production bundle installation. The tiny fixture is useful for failure tests but cannot establish production tokenization cost.

## Desired state

Phase 1 produces a pinned production-bundle measurement that separates sequential validation tokenization, FastEmbed tokenization, ORT inference, vector validation, and lock/permit wait. Before treatment collection, `/statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` must define what improvement would matter for the target workloads. Phase 2 runs only if the fresh evidence supports that predeclared claim; without a repository performance policy, report evidence and obtain a human change gate rather than inventing a threshold.

If the gate passes, preserve input-versus-invariant taxonomy while avoiding the repeated successful tokenization pass. Preferred minimum design to test:

1. Map FastEmbed tokenization failures to `InferenceError::Input` rather than lane-failing `Invariant`.
2. During `Backend::load`, probe the hash-pinned tokenizer with empty/whitespace input and record whether special-token processing guarantees a non-empty encoding.
3. Skip the per-request pre-pass only when the stable bundle probe proves zero-token output impossible. Otherwise retain the existing guard.

Do not add a public knob, model abstraction, tokenizer cache, or unbounded encoding cache.

## Required skills and execution order

1. `/quantitative-analysis:statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` freezes phase boundaries, workload classes, warm/cold state, service-time outcome, bundle population, and reporting contract.
2. `/quantitative-analysis:benchmark-experiment-design` fixes process-level units, treatment order, A/A path, replication, intervals, and stopping before collection.
3. `/performance:perf-pipeline` coordinates attribution, verifies the model path is the actual bottleneck, and gates any source change on measured evidence.
4. `/performance:performance-analyzer` checks duplicate work, allocations, lock hold, and copy frequency at current HEAD.
5. `/performance:tokio-runtime-profiling` is conditional if permit wait, blocking-pool delay, or worker starvation contaminates tokenization attribution.
6. `/performance:simd-optimize` is conditional only if a measured tokenizer leaf kernel remains hot after eliminating duplicate work. Do not add custom SIMD or CPU dispatch in this task.
7. `/low-level-systems:systems-data-structures` is conditional only if a proposal retains or caches batch encodings. It must then account for cardinality, residency, ownership, bounds, and failure. Default is no retained structure.
8. `/testing:test-strategy` owns failure-taxonomy, lane-lifecycle, memory-bound, and vector-parity tests. `/implementation:rust-implementation` applies the selected minimal change.

## Measurement contract

- Artifact: exact production bundle manifest/fingerprint/model hash, ORT library hash/version, commit, rustc, CPU affinity/cgroup, host load.
- Workloads: batch rows `{1,16,64}` crossed with representative token-length strata from real compartment/memory/commit text, plus 1 KiB, 32 KiB, and 128 KiB synthetic controls.
- Outcomes: wall service time while holding the model lock, validation-tokenization CPU, FastEmbed tokenization CPU, ORT CPU, allocations/peak RSS, successful items, input errors, invariant errors.
- Treatments: current double pass, taxonomy-only refactor with pass retained, probe-gated pass removal. Include current versus current A/A.
- At least three pilot process blocks, then fixed independent block count from pilot variance. Randomize complete treatment order. Requests inside one process are subsamples.
- Report absolute time, paired ratio and interval, process count, run failures, and workload-stratified results. Do not report one aggregate across text lengths.

## Files

- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs`: `Backend::load`, `Backend::embed`, FastEmbed error mapping, stable tokenizer probe.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs`: read-only unless taxonomy mapping requires a narrowly scoped match update; preserve `settle_inference` lane-failing rules for genuine invariants.
- `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_bundle.rs`: bundle-load/probe cases.
- `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_protocol.rs` and `synapse_roundtrip.rs`: request-level error and vector behavior.
- Add a focused benchmark under `crates/mc-host/benches/` or `examples/` only after the claim and experiment design are frozen.
- `docs/perf/`: retained run manifest and report.

## Test strategy

- Empty text remains rejected as input.
- Whitespace-only and zero-token-producing inputs return a request-scoped input/schema error and leave lane health Ready.
- Deliberate tokenizer failure never becomes `Invariant` and never marks the lane failing.
- Genuine model/output invariant failures still mark the lane failing before results can escape.
- Valid corpus vectors remain within existing tolerance and item ordering is unchanged.
- Probe result is stable for the loaded hash-pinned tokenizer and does not run per request.
- Allocation/peak-memory test proves candidate does not retain batch-sized encodings outside resident accounting.
- Shutdown still joins started native work and releases model state in existing order.

## Stop conditions

- If the fresh evidence does not support the predeclared materiality claim, close as measured-and-rejected. Do not change the guard.
- Stop if the production bundle or ORT identity cannot be pinned.
- Stop if failure taxonomy cannot be preserved without changing FastEmbed internals or broad lane-failure semantics.
- Reject any candidate that increases peak uncharged memory, stores encodings across calls, changes vectors, or weakens lane condemnation for genuine invariants.
- No custom tokenizer, SIMD kernel, or model wrapper in this task.

## Related work

- `magic-context-18r`: sibling hash and depth-scanner reductions.
- `magic-context-ioi`: concurrency experiment consumes the measured service-time split; collections must use one pinned commit or rebaseline.
- `magic-context-s64`: query admission and polling changes can alter observed queue wait but not tokenizer service demand.
- `magic-context-c50.8`: production bundle provenance prerequisite.
- `magic-context-515`: originating performance audit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Production bundle, ORT, commit, host, workload, and process-level experiment design are pinned before measurement.
- [ ] Baseline report separates validation tokenization, FastEmbed tokenization, ORT inference, permit/lock wait, allocations, and outcomes by workload stratum.
- [ ] Source changes occur only after the fresh experiment supports the frozen claim and a human approves the change; absent a repository policy, no automatic pass/fail threshold is invented.
- [ ] If changed, FastEmbed tokenization failures map to `InferenceError::Input`; zero-token behavior is decided by a one-time bundle probe; genuine invariants retain lane-failing behavior.
- [ ] No batch-sized retained encoding structure or uncharged-memory increase is introduced.
- [ ] Empty, whitespace, tokenizer-failure, invariant-failure, vector-parity, allocation, and shutdown tests pass.
- [ ] `cargo test -p mc-host`, `cargo clippy -p mc-host --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- [ ] `docs/perf/` records either a justified minimal implementation with before/after bounds or a measured rejection with no production code change.
acceptance_criteria: Production-bundle profile isolates validation tokenization from FastEmbed and ORT; source changes require frozen-claim evidence plus human approval; any change preserves input/invariant taxonomy, lane health, vector parity, and resident-memory bounds.

title: Benchmark configurable Synapse inference concurrency
description:
Synapse serializes all inference: one CPU permit (`crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:171`,
constructed `Semaphore::new(1)` at `:199` and `:224`), one query-admission permit (`:174`),
and one ORT intra-op thread (`crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:255`). This task
produces a **measurement report and a decision**, not a knob. No production concurrency
parameter is added unless this experiment selects one.

## Mechanisms already established by code reading (to be quantified, not re-derived)

- `Backend::embed` takes `Mutex<TextEmbedding>` (`inference.rs:181`, lock at `:277`), so
  extra CPU permits over one `Backend` cannot parallelize anything; they only move waiting
  from the FIFO semaphore into an unfair `std::sync::Mutex`.
- Batch workers are spawned at admission (`mod.rs:638`) and queue on the *same* FIFO
  `cpu` semaphore as queries (`mod.rs:514`, `:646`). With `max_queued_jobs: 64` and
  `max_batch_items: 64` (`mod.rs:69`, `:71`), one query can wait behind up to 64 full
  batches. This head-of-line coupling — not the absence of parallelism — is the primary
  suspect for query tail under batch load.
- The query-admission permit is held by the worker through the native call, past the
  request deadline (`mod.rs:478-497`), so a timed-out query keeps the query lane closed
  until its native call finishes; a second concurrent query gets `queue_full` (pinned by
  `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_protocol.rs:90`).
- Per-text validation tokenization runs *inside* the model lock (`inference.rs:281-296`)
  before fastembed tokenizes again, so service demand today includes duplicated work
  (owned by `magic-context-chj`; `magic-context-18r` owns only hash/depth preprocessing).

## Phase 0 — prerequisites (blocking; no production source edits)

**0a. Production model artifact provenance.** No production bundle exists in-repo; only
`crates/mc-host/tests/fixtures/synapse-tiny` (8 dims, WordLevel tokenizer), which
`docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` §5 states cannot certify the production model. Installation
is owned by magic-context-c50.8 (in progress). Before any collection, record: bundle
directory, `manifest.model`, `fingerprint`, `dims`, `max_tokens`, `pooling`,
`quantization`, `recommended_batch{rows,token_budget}`, `model_file.sha256`,
`corpus.sha256`, `manifest.provenance`, plus ORT library path, version, target triple and
the pinned `ort_library_sha256` (`SynapseConfig`, `mod.rs:89`). The TypeScript default
local model is `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`
(`packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts:22`); if the Synapse bundle is a
different embedding space, say so — results do not transfer across fingerprints.

**0b. Observability prerequisite.** `magic-context-a52` owns the bounded, fixed-cardinality
Synapse snapshot for CPU-permit wait/hold, native inference time, rejection reason, poll outcome,
and queue/job depth. This experiment is blocked until that contract lands and its overhead is
measured. Harness-side scheduled-send and terminal accounting remains independent. Resource series
come from `/proc/<pid>/status` (`VmRSS`, `VmHWM`), `/proc/<pid>/stat` utime/stime deltas, and
`pidstat -t`. If blocking-pool versus executor delay remains unresolved, invoke
`/performance:tokio-runtime-profiling`; enable `tokio_unstable` only in the measurement artifact,
not as an unreviewed production build change.

**0c. Generator.** `crates/mc-host/examples/perf_load.rs` speaks only `perf-echo`; it has
no `embed.query`/`embed.batch`/`embed.result` arm. Extend it (or add a sibling) reusing its
coordinated-omission-honest accounting (scheduled-send boundary, per-code error map,
scheduler lag) and the `scripts/perf-mc-host.sh` run layout. Store mergeable histograms or
raw sorted vectors; never average percentiles.

## Claim and outcomes

Claim to decide: *for the pinned production bundle, on the target host class, topology T
delivers materially lower query p99 under batch load and/or higher batch deadline goodput
than the single-permit baseline, at a stated RSS/CPU cost, without weakening any bound or
lifecycle guarantee.*

Primary outcome family (declared before collection, two members):
1. query logical-request latency p50/p95/p99, boundary = scheduled send → terminal frame;
2. batch deadline goodput = items published within the client freshness deadline / elapsed.

Every level reports intended / scheduled / sent / admitted / completed / `queue_full` /
`timeout` / `cancelled` counts and `deadline_success_fraction`. Timeouts and rejections are
never dropped from latency; `queue_full` is not goodput. Exploratory: batch job latency,
poll count per job, CPU-seconds per 1k items, RSS peak, shutdown drain time.

## Workload and arrival semantics

- **Query arm — open.** Exogenous fixed-rate scheduled arrivals (interactive search does
  not wait for prior completions), sweep offered λ. Run two variants: no-retry (clean
  rejection accounting) and client-retry-modeled (~100 ms backoff as magic-context-s64
  describes), reporting attempt vs logical-request latency separately.
- **Batch arm — partly open.** Indexing sessions arrive exogenously; within a session,
  chunks are completion-coupled (submit → poll → next). Pin rows per job at
  `recommended_batch.rows` plus {1, 16, 64}; draw token lengths from a real corpus sample.
  fastembed pads each chunk to its longest encoding
  (`fastembed-6.0.0/src/text_embedding/impl.rs:359-372`), so service time scales with
  rows × padded length. Stratify results by token-length class; do not merge classes.
- **Mixed arm — the deciding arm.** Batch submissions at fixed rate + low-rate open query
  load: the head-of-line case created by the shared FIFO permit.
- Warmup: discard the first 10% of the window (baseline contract) and *verify* steady
  state (flat permit-wait, flat RSS), not a fixed iteration count. Ramp down and confirm
  recovery.

## Model and host population

Generalization target is developer machines running the plugin (README: macOS/Windows/
Linux; Synapse itself is Linux-only — `ensure_ort` fails closed elsewhere). The available
box is 128 CPU / 246 GB with 1-minute load spiking above 100, the same hazard
`docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md` records for Collection 1 — unrepresentative and noisy.
Run every arm inside a pinned CPU budget emulating the target classes: cgroup v2 `cpu.max`
or `taskset`/cpuset at **4, 8, 16** logical CPUs, plus one unrestricted run labeled
exploratory. At 4 CPUs also run a co-tenancy arm with a fixed background CPU load (the
editor/agent the host shares the machine with). Record per run: cores, `cpu.max`, load
before/after, kernel, rustc, commit, ORT sha256, bundle fingerprint.

## Configurations to compare, and rejection conditions

- **B0 baseline** — as-is (cpu 1, query admission 1, intra-op 1). Also the "do nothing"
  candidate: magic-context-s64's admission/backoff fix may close the tail with no
  concurrency change at all.
- **T1 ORT intra-op parallelism** — `with_intra_threads(n)` for n ∈ {2,4,cores}, one call
  at a time (`inference.rs:255` is the only touched line; no weight duplication, no
  lifecycle change). *Reject if:* the fresh bounds do not support the frozen throughput/latency
  claim; post-burst idle CPU or query tails move adversely for the target host class — ORT exposes
  `session.intra_op.allow_spinning` (`ort-2.0.0-rc.13/src/session/builder/impl_config_keys.rs:96`)
  but fastembed's `InitOptionsUserDefined` does not, so spin-wait cannot be disabled
  without bypassing fastembed's builder; or query p99 regresses at the 4-CPU budget from
  ORT threads competing with tokio workers.
- **T2 separate query and batch lanes** — reserve one permit class for queries so queries
  stop queueing behind up to 64 batches. No added parallelism; directly targets the
  measured mechanism; testable with the deterministic engine too. *Reject if* B0's query
  p99 under batch load already meets the target.
- **T3 chunk-level permit release** — batch worker embeds in `recommended_batch`-sized
  chunks, releasing and re-acquiring the permit between chunks to bound head-of-line
  delay. *Reject if* chunking costs material throughput (padding/session overhead) or
  cannot preserve `AbandonGuard` publication semantics (`mod.rs:664-688`).
- **T4 model-instance pool (N backends)** — the only true parallel-inference option.
  *Reject if:* RSS scales ≈N× — weights are deliberately moved into the model once to
  avoid duplicate buffers (`inference.rs:192-196`; bundle cap `MAX_MODEL_BYTES` 2 GiB,
  `bundle.rs:18`) — or startup probe+certification cost ×N is unacceptable, or the 4-CPU
  target cannot pay the footprint.
- **T5 more permits over one backend** — rejected by construction (`Backend` mutex,
  `inference.rs:277`); include only as a control run if the arithmetic must be shown.

## Cost, queue depth, and capacity bound

Per config and per CPU budget: steady `VmRSS`, `VmHWM`, RSS after 60 s idle (arena
retention), CPU-seconds per 1k items, idle CPU for 60 s after the last request, thread
count and per-thread CPU, shutdown drain time. Compute per-resource service demand
`D_cpu` (busy CPU-seconds per completed item) and report the necessary bound
`X ≤ c/D_cpu`; treat it as an upper bound, never an achievable throughput. Do **not** use
`%util` as saturation on a multi-core host — report queue depth plus latency at fixed
offered load. Check Little's Law `E[L] = λ_eff·E[W]` using *admitted* throughput: the query
path is a loss system (fail-fast `queue_full`), the batch path a finite-capacity queue
(K = `max_queued_jobs` 64, server = the FIFO permit). Never convert a mean occupancy into
a permit count; if an overload model is quoted, name it and its invalidators (deterministic
deadlines, retries, non-Poisson arrivals).

## USL applicability

Not applicable to the open query and mixed arms — use the offered-load/goodput curve and
the service-demand bound instead. Admissible only for closed one-request-in-flight sweeps:
T1 over intra-op threads, T4 over pool size with N in-flight batches. Even then require ≥6
levels, independent repeats, randomized order, identical text mix at every level, and
report σ/κ with CIs; refuse coefficient interpretation if residuals show a breakpoint, a
term's CI covers zero (drop to the nested model), error rates move with N, or the fitted
peak lies beyond the measured range.

## A/A control, replication, stopping

- **A/A:** run B0 against B0 through both labels and both schedule slots with an identical
  binary. Report mechanical integrity (binary sha256, bundle fingerprint, ORT sha, run
  completeness) separately from null calibration. `/benchmark-experiment-design` sets the number
  of complete null blocks needed for the chosen statistic. One observed A/A range is not a
  "noise floor".
- **Units:** treatment applied per host process invocation; a block is one complete ordered
  set of configs; the analysis unit is one complete block contrast; requests are
  subsamples. Reset between letters: fresh process, fresh bundle load, fixed idle gap,
  recorded load average. The shared box is the interference boundary.
- **Assignment:** seed-recorded restricted randomization over ABBA-style complete
  templates, template counts differing by at most one. Retain every failed or aborted run —
  a timeout, OOM, or lane-failing outcome may be treatment-dependent.
- **Sizing/stopping:** 3 pilot blocks for paired log-contrast variance, then a fixed block
  count from that pilot; inspect only after a complete block. Two primary outcomes →
  Bonferroni/Holm across the declared family; all other metrics exploratory.

## Required skills and execution order

1. `/quantitative-analysis:statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` freezes logical request, attempt, service-time, response-time, arrival, outcome, warmup, workload mix, host population, and goodput semantics.
2. `/quantitative-analysis:benchmark-experiment-design` freezes treatment application, randomization and analysis units, A/A controls, block order, replication, uncertainty construction, multiplicity, and stopping before inspecting treatment results.
3. `/performance:perf-pipeline` coordinates baseline, model/runtime/host attribution, specialist routing, human gate before any topology change, and equivalent post-change verification.
4. `/performance:load-test-harness` owns open-loop query and mixed-load sweeps, scheduled-send latency, generator headroom, saturation knee, and recovery ramp-down.
5. `/quantitative-analysis:queueing-theory-for-engineers` consumes the measured arrival and service-demand model to calculate stability, finite-capacity blocking/wait, Little's Law checks, and candidate bounds. It does not choose runtime full behavior.
6. `/quantitative-analysis:usl-scalability-analysis` is allowed only for valid closed-concurrency sweeps with at least six levels and independent repeats. It is not valid for open query or mixed arms.
7. `/performance:tokio-runtime-profiling` separates CPU-permit wait, blocking-pool delay, worker starvation, and work-steal imbalance before blaming model concurrency.
8. `/low-level-systems:scalable-concurrency` owns any selected ownership/topology change. `/low-level-systems:systems-data-structures` is conditional if a permit queue, model pool, or job representation is redesigned; no structure is selected from Big-O alone.
9. `/systems-design:bounded-design` guards capacity, behavior at full, cancellation, deadline, fairness, recovery, and shutdown. `/testing:test-strategy` chooses lifecycle and concurrency tests.
10. `/performance:bench-compare` runs the frozen exact-artifact schedule. No repository pass/fail claim is made without a separately authored performance policy.

## Correctness and lifecycle guards (must hold for any selected topology)

Lane-failure check after permit acquisition and before using a captured backend
(`mod.rs:526`, `:653`); `settle_inference` marking the lane failing before any error
reaches a sink; `AbandonGuard` publication (`mod.rs:664-688`); ordered shutdown
`closing.cancel → close_admission → tracker.close → tracker.wait` (`mod.rs:920-926`) —
report drain time, since N concurrent native calls extend worst case to N × service time;
resident-byte charges held across the native call (`mod.rs:495-497`) unchanged; no starvation
of either request class. Existing guards that constrain any change:
`tests/synapse_protocol.rs:90` (query overload preserves tool-provider capacity) and
`tests/synapse_jobs.rs:446` (graceful shutdown with queued/running/retained jobs).

## Confounds and ordering

Pin one commit for all arms. `magic-context-18r` changes parse/hash demand,
`magic-context-chj` may change tokenization demand, and `magic-context-s64` changes query
admission/poll cadence; any landing mid-collection invalidates cross-config comparison. Record all
three states in the run manifest and rebaseline after any change.

## Stop conditions

Stop and report without adding a knob when any prerequisite is missing: production bundle/ORT identity cannot be pinned; `magic-context-a52` attribution is unavailable or fails its overhead review; the load generator cannot maintain scheduled open load; A/A shows path asymmetry or unstable null behavior; request mix, errors, or service demand change across concurrency levels; or the target host population is undefined. Reject candidates that move waiting behind the `Backend` mutex, exceed resident/RSS or shutdown budgets, starve queries or batches, weaken lane-failure/cancellation invariants, or need unbounded queues. USL coefficient interpretation stops when its applicability checks fail. Without a separately authored repository performance policy, the task ends with evidence and a human decision, not an automatic production change.

## Related work

- `magic-context-a52` blocks measurement: Synapse wait/hold/inference/rejection/poll/depth snapshot.
- `magic-context-c50.8` blocks production artifact/runtime provenance.
- `magic-context-s64` is related: admission/retry/poll policy changes mixed-load results and queue topology.
- `magic-context-18r` changes parse/hash service demand; `magic-context-chj` may change tokenization demand.
- `magic-context-515` is the closed originating audit and model-free baseline.
- `magic-context-bx3` is future GPU work and must not be pulled into this CPU experiment.

## Commands (harness lands in Phase 0)

```
cargo build --release -p mc-host --examples
MC_SYNAPSE_TEST_ORT_LIBRARY=<lib> target/release/examples/synapse_host <data> <bundle> <lib> <sha256>
taskset -c 0-3 ...   # or: systemd-run --user -p AllowedCPUs=0-3 ...
scripts/perf-mc-host.sh docs/perf/runs/synapse-<config> <arm> ...
python <skill>/scripts/exp_design.py size --design paired-log --pilot-contrasts contrasts.csv \
  --null-ratio <claim-owned-boundary> --alternative-ratio <claim-owned-alternative> \
  --alpha <family-allocation> --power <declared-power> --sided <bound-direction>
```

Raw logs plus `env.txt` under `docs/perf/runs/<config>/`; report alongside
`docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md`.

## Acceptance

A report in `docs/perf/` that: pins bundle fingerprint, ORT identity, commit and CPU
budgets; passes the A/A mechanical and calibration control; reports per config and per CPU
budget the offered/admitted/completed/`queue_full`/timeout counts, query p50/p95/p99 on the
scheduled-send boundary, batch deadline goodput, queue-depth series, CPU-seconds per 1k
items, RSS steady/peak/idle, and shutdown drain; states `X ≤ c/D_cpu`; declares USL
applicability per arm; and ends with one decision — retain the single permit, or adopt
exactly one named topology with its full bound contract (unit, scope, capacity, behavior at
full, wait bound, client-visible feedback code, recovery) and the guard tests it requires.
No production concurrency knob is added unless this report selects one.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned production-bundle experiment with valid A/A, arrival semantics, process-level design, queueing/USL applicability, runtime attribution, CPU/RSS/shutdown costs, and mixed query/batch outcomes produces an evidence-only decision; no concurrency knob lands unless separately approved.
notes:
Stays deferred: still requires production bundle evidence (magic-context-c50.8) and is not the next move. s64 (retry jitter + fast-first polling) proceeds first; any concurrency topology change here forces re-derivation of s64's queue models.
2026-08-28 decision complete. Six valid release-profile runs at artifact 3cea1b14657c809cbfc0d7b92126f76265b08043+patch-551c83cfb1ffc5a4. T2 failed the predeclared adoption rule: unchanged batch goodput, mixed p99, and worse query outcome rates in separate repetitions. Retain B0; no production concurrency code. PR #80 rewritten docs-only at 7fa2e87f. Evidence: docs/perf/synapse-concurrency-decision.md; raw local target/synapse-concurrency-bge-decision-final/.
PR #80 feedback disposition: original broad acceptance matrix was not completed and is not claimed. The task is closed only for the scoped matched-width T2 question. Production artifact, A/A, multi-budget, RSS, CPU, and shutdown confirmation moved to magic-context-w4g / magic-context-bux; docs/perf/synapse-scheduling-architecture-decision.md supersedes T2 as forward architecture guidance.

title: Eliminate duplicate Synapse hashing and scalar depth scan
description:
# Eliminate duplicate Synapse hashing and scalar depth scan

Verified against `feat/broca-runner-route` @ `f5f3c463` (synapse sources identical to the reviewed tree). Two *localized, semantics-preserving*
CPU reductions on the Synapse request path. The tokenizer sub-finding is **split out** (see
"Split-out" below) because it needs a real bundle to measure and changes failure taxonomy.

## Verified sub-findings

| # | Site | Fact | Measured cost (this host, 8 MiB batch body) |
|---|------|------|--------------------------------------------|
| B | `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/jobs.rs:180-194` `digest_payload` hashes `item.text` | second full-text SHA-256; first is `protocol.rs:796` `sha256_hex(raw.0.text)` | 4.61 ms of the 4.61 ms digest (99.9%) |
| C | `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/protocol.rs:541-560` string skip uses `iter().position(\|b\| b==b'"' \|\| b==b'\\')` | scalar 2.5 GB/s; `memchr2` is 3-38x faster and already in the dep graph | 3.42 ms -> 90.7 us |

`depth_exceeds` runs on **every** synapse request (`mod.rs:815` -> `protocol.rs:582`), bodies up
to `MAX_BODY_BYTES` = 32 MiB. `digest_payload` runs on every `embed.batch` admission
(`jobs.rs:355`, computed before the table lock). Combined removable CPU on a max-size batch:
~8 ms per request, single-threaded, on the async handler.

## B - drop the text term from the admission digest

### Semantic invariant (oracle)
`payload_digest` decides `Conflict` vs `Existing` at `jobs.rs:375`. Requirement: *two
admissions sharing a `request_key` must produce equal digests iff their payloads are
identical.* Every production admission passes `mod.rs:584`, which rejects
`request_key != canonical_key`, and `canonical_request_key` (`protocol.rs:846-882`) already
binds model, fingerprint, epoch, ordered ids and ordered **recomputed** content hashes. Each
`content_sha256` is recomputed from the text and compared at `protocol.rs:796-799`, so
`content_sha256 == SHA256(text)` holds for every `BatchItem` the protocol builds. Therefore
digesting `(key, id, content_sha256)` per item distinguishes exactly the same payload pairs as
today's digest, unless SHA-256 collides - the same assumption the content-identity ledger
already rests on.

### Minimum change
Delete `update(item.text.as_bytes());` (`jobs.rs:190`) and extend the `digest_payload` doc
comment with the invariant above (recomputed hash stands in for the text; length-prefixed
framing stays, so id/hash boundaries remain unambiguous). No signature, no type, no call-site
change. Expected diff: 1 line of code + comment.

### Guards
- Keep the length prefix (`hasher.update(len.to_le_bytes())`) - removing it would let
  `("ab","c")` alias `("a","bc")`.
- Do **not** delete the digest entirely: `JobTable` is a self-contained unit reached by
  `admit_uncharged_for_tests` and must not assume the caller ran the canonical check.
- Do not touch `canonical_request_key`: it is a cross-language contract with
  `getSynapseBatchRequestKey` (golden vectors in
  `protocol.rs::request_key_matches_the_javascript_golden_vectors`).

### Tests
- Existing must pass unchanged: `synapse::jobs::tests` (replay/conflict/closed at `jobs.rs:865-915`), `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_jobs.rs`,
  `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_protocol.rs:521-545` (conflict matrix), `synapse_roundtrip.rs`.
- Add one unit test in `jobs.rs::tests`: same key, same ids, **different `content_sha256`**
  -> `AdmitOutcome::Conflict`; byte-identical items -> `AdmitOutcome::Existing`. The existing
  conflict case differs only in id/text with a constant `"0".repeat(64)` hash, so it does not
  pin the post-change discriminator.

## C - `memchr2` for the in-string skip

### Semantic invariant (oracle)
`depth_exceeds` must stay byte-identical in verdict to today for every input, including:
delimiters inside strings never count; backslash consumes exactly one following byte
(parity); an unterminated string returns `false` and leaves syntax reporting to serde; keys
count like values; scalars count one level below their container.

### Minimum change
Add `memchr = "2"` to `crates/mc-host/Cargo.toml` (**already in `Cargo.lock` as 2.8.2 via
`serde_json`** - no new crate in the graph, no new build unit) and replace the inner
`body[index..].iter().position(...)` (`protocol.rs:542-545`) with `memchr::memchr2(b'"', b'\\', &body[index..])`.
Nothing else: the outer structural dispatch runs only at token boundaries, and for
`embed.batch` bodies almost every byte is inside a string, so one call covers the bulk.
`index == body.len()` yields an empty slice, which `memchr2` handles. Expected diff: 1 dep
line + 1 expression.

### Tests
Existing `protocol.rs::tests` depth cases (`depth_eight_passes_and_depth_nine_fails`,
`delimiters_inside_strings_never_count_toward_depth`,
`a_scalar_at_the_container_limit_is_one_level_deeper`,
`depth_counts_params_that_precede_method`) plus `tests/protocol_vectors.rs`. Add a
differential property test (loop over ~10k pseudo-random bodies from a seeded LCG over the
alphabet `{ } [ ] " \ , : space x \n }`) asserting the retained scalar reference and the
`memchr2` version agree; keep the reference `fn` in `#[cfg(test)]` so the oracle is permanent.
Seed printed on failure. This is the check that a hand-audited escape-parity change needs.

## Benchmark protocol (both sub-findings)

- **Harness**: one new `crates/mc-host/benches/synapse_preprocess.rs`. No new dependency:
  `criterion` is absent from the workspace and is not needed for two kernels. Use a
  `#[bench]`-free plain `fn main` bench binary (`[[bench]] harness = false`) with
  `Instant`, `std::hint::black_box`, raw block output, artifact hashes, and environment metadata.
- **Design**: `/benchmark-experiment-design` fixes warmup evidence, treatment order, process-level
  analysis units, independent block count, interval construction, and stopping before fresh
  collection. Repetitions inside one process are subsamples and cannot expose build/allocator/layout
  effects. Report absolute values, paired ratios and uncertainty, not only a best/min time.
- **Treatments**: (1) scalar baseline = today's code, (2) candidate. For B also record
  (3) `hashes-only digest` vs (4) `no digest at all` as a floor, to show the residual is
  ~1 us and not worth further work.
- **Workloads (size classes)**: 756 B single-item body; 64 KiB / 16 items x 4 KiB (typical
  chunk mix); 8 MiB / 64 items x 128 KiB (`max_batch_text_bytes` shape); one escape-dense
  variant (`\n` every 64 B) as the adversarial case for C - escapes bound the win at ~4.8x.
- **Baselines to beat, not skip**: scalar `position` (C), `sha2` at its SHA-NI rate
  (B: 1.82 GB/s measured, so the digest is already hardware-fast - the win is *not hashing
  the text at all*, never a faster hash). Do not swap SHA-256, do not add `asm`/`force-soft`
  features, do not evaluate non-cryptographic hashes: the digest output feeds an identity
  decision and the content hash is a wire contract.
- **Allocation / copy measures**: assert in the bench binary with a counting
  `GlobalAlloc` wrapper that (a) `depth_exceeds` performs **zero** allocations before and
  after, (b) `digest_payload` performs zero, (c) no additional byte copy of item text is
  introduced anywhere. Also record peak RSS delta for the 8 MiB case; both changes must be
  RSS-neutral (they only *remove* reads).
- **Decision and stop conditions**:
  - Freeze the workload-specific materiality claim and smallest important effect before fresh
    treatment collection. The pilot numbers above may size the experiment but must not become a
    post-hoc repository policy.
  - For C, report the full size/escape distribution and uncertainty. Stop if small-body cost moves in
    the wrong direction or the maintained-library path does not improve representative large bodies.
  - For B, stop if any idempotency verdict changes or the fresh run does not show that removing the
    second text pass reduces representative batch CPU.
  - Without a separately authored repository performance policy, present evidence for human approval;
    do not auto-classify a pass from an invented percentage.
  - Either sub-finding being rejected does **not** block the other; land only approved work.
  - No further optimization of these two functions after their gate passes. Do not proceed to
    a vectorized structural scanner, a SIMD JSON depth pass, hand-written intrinsics,
    `#[target_feature]`, or runtime dispatch. Those require a *new* representative profile and the
    `/simd-optimize` need, population, and amortization gates. `memchr` already carries SSE2/AVX2 and
    NEON dispatch; a custom kernel would duplicate maintained code and add an unsafe-review
    burden for no measured need.

## Required skills and execution order

1. `/performance:perf-pipeline` owns orchestration, baseline provenance, evidence routing, and final verification. Static findings remain hypotheses until the frozen microbench confirms them.
2. `/quantitative-analysis:statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` freezes workload classes, timing boundary, warm/cold state, outcomes, estimand, target host population, and reporting contract before collection.
3. `/quantitative-analysis:benchmark-experiment-design` fixes process-level units, A/B order, A/A control, replication, interval construction, and stopping. Inner iterations are subsamples, not independent runs.
4. `/performance:performance-analyzer` rechecks frequency, allocation, copy, and async-worker impact at current HEAD before editing.
5. `/performance:hashing-prng-and-checksum-speed` owns the SHA-256 semantic contract and verifies that the win comes from removing the redundant text pass, not weakening the stable cryptographic identity.
6. `/performance:simd-optimize` owns the depth-scanner implementation level. Its zero-dispatch ladder applies: use maintained `memchr2`; custom intrinsics, `#[target_feature]`, or runtime dispatch are forbidden unless a new post-change profile passes need, population, and amortization gates.
7. `/low-level-systems:systems-data-structures` is conditional only. Invoke it if implementation proposes changing `BatchItem`, `JobTable`, indexing, or resident layout. Current localized changes do not justify a representation redesign.
8. `/testing:test-strategy` selects differential/property and protocol integration tests; `/implementation:rust-implementation` applies the approved minimal edits.

## Portability
`memchr` 2.8.2: `std` + runtime x86-64 SSE2/AVX2 and aarch64 NEON dispatch with a portable
fallback, so no `RUSTFLAGS`, no `target-cpu`, no `cfg` fork, and no behavioural difference
across hosts. `sha2` 0.10.9 already autodetects SHA-NI through `cpufeatures`; both changes are
arch-neutral. Numbers above are from AMD EPYC 9R14 (Zen 4, sha_ni/avx2/avx512f), rustc 1.97.1,
`-O`; on a host without AVX2 expect a different ratio; the fresh target-host run reports it without assuming a fixed speedup.

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope; do not bundle)
- Tokenizer pre-pass, tracked separately by `magic-context-chj`.
- `sha256_hex` hex formatting (`protocol.rs:888-895`, 32 `write!` calls) and
  `canonical_request_key`'s two `json_string` allocations per item. Measured: hex encoding is
  451 ns of the 1612 ns spent hashing one 2 KiB chunk (28%); a safe lookup-table encode is
  45.6 ns. Real but a constant factor, not a duplicate pass. File separately if wanted; the
  golden-vector tests already cover it, so it is ~5 lines with no new test burden.
- No change to `parse_reservation_bytes` or the resident-byte ledger: neither change alters
  peak allocation, so the reservation constants stay valid.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `digest_payload` no longer reads `item.text`; its doc comment states the
   recomputed-hash invariant.
2. `depth_exceeds` uses `memchr::memchr2`; `memchr` is a direct dependency and
   `Cargo.lock` gains **no** new package.
3. `cargo test -p mc-host` passes with no expectation edited except the added tests;
   `cargo clippy -p mc-host --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.
4. New tests: (a) digest conflict discriminated by `content_sha256`, (b) seeded differential
   property test scalar-vs-`memchr2` over >= 10k random bodies.
5. `crates/mc-host/benches/synapse_preprocess.rs` committed, reporting for each size class:
   treatment medians, paired ratio + bootstrap CI, process count, allocation counts, host,
   commit, rustc version. Fresh evidence and the human decision are recorded in the task note.
6. No behaviour change observable on the wire: `synapse_protocol.rs`, `synapse_jobs.rs`,
   `synapse_roundtrip.rs`, `protocol_vectors.rs` unchanged and green.

## Related work

- `magic-context-chj`: split-out production-bundle measurement and safe tokenization change.
- `magic-context-a52`: Synapse wait/hold/inference attribution consumed by later whole-request analysis.
- `magic-context-ioi`: concurrency experiment must pin whether this task landed and rebaseline if needed.
- `magic-context-vho`: resident parse accounting is separate and must not be changed here.
- `magic-context-515`: originating performance audit.
