title: mc-host: anchor lifecycle transaction lock to the evidence namespace
description:
Codex review of PR #21 (comment 3837084109): the KTD2 lifecycle-root lock inode is a mutual-exclusion token only. If ${dataDir}/cortexkit/lifecycle is renamed while a transaction holds the lock, a second caller recreates the path and locks a fresh inode, and two mutating transactions overlap on the same sibling run/ evidence — the lock descriptor anchors no evidence operations.

Blast radius today is bounded: no production mutator takes acquire_exclusive yet (launcher work is U2+, gated on c50.12/c50.4), and the evidence writes are individually fenced (instance lock + atomic identity-fenced writes), which is also why probes tolerate running with no root lock. But the serialization guarantee the doc claims for future launcher transactions does not survive path replacement.

Fix direction: make mutating transactions operate through a descriptor anchored by the locked inode (e.g. lock the runtime directory inode itself, or resolve evidence paths relative to the locked directory and re-verify identity), and update protocol 4.3 accordingly. Should land with or before the first production acquire_exclusive caller (U2+).

title: Revert-aligned kernel visibility and abandonment capsules
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` (R1, R3–R5, R7–R8; KTD7). Kernel-store dependency: `magic-context-kh8.2`.

## Goal
When a host reverts a session to message M, prevent semantic state derived from the abandoned suffix from entering later prompts while retaining an auditable abandonment capsule.

## Scope
1. Determine a reliable revert signal for each supported host. If no signal can be distinguished safely, do nothing.
2. Map message-source spans to kernel commit boundaries.
3. On revert, append one daemon-owned commit that ends suffix eligibility, withdraws suffix staging state, emits derived invalidations, and writes one typed abandonment event containing the boundary, abandoned span, last plan or todo snapshot, and tool-failure tail when present.
4. Keep earlier `known_as_of` snapshots and historical records recoverable.
5. Route notes and user-memory changes through their existing Rust-owned surfaces and kernel commit semantics.

No execution DAG, environment snapshot, side-effect compensator, or workspace rollback belongs here.
design: Persist source-span-to-commit provenance. Revert appends correction, validity, and abandonment events in a new commit rather than resetting commit sequence.
acceptance_criteria: Each host has documented signal and false-positive no-op behavior; suffix-only objects cannot reach automatic injection after revert; earlier known_as_of reads remain reproducible; notes, user memories, and historian output obey the boundary; one capsule is written per idempotency key; derived invalidation preserves the prefix; no semantic or user data is physically deleted.
notes: Scope is Magic Context state only. Harness workspace and conversation restoration remain host responsibilities.

title: Speculative recall prefetch during long tool calls (instrument + flag-gated prototype)
description:
## Context

Long tool calls (`cargo test`, builds, dependency downloads) leave a multi-second idle window where the main model waits. MC computes recall on the turn path today. This task hides recall latency and widens recall quality by pre-warming retrieval during that window, using the tool call itself as the query seed.

Origin: accepted item #1 from the 2026-08-22 speculative-execution brainstorm review. The wider proposal (advisory LLM branches, EV scheduler, speculative tool execution, KV transfer) was **rejected**; this task is deliberately the deterministic-retrieval-only slice. Do not scope-creep toward LLM speculation.

## Current State

- Recall/injection happens per turn: `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/inject-compartments.ts` (utility-tier assignment ~line 238), budgeted by `DEFAULT_MEMORY_BUDGET_TOKENS` (4k twin in `crates/mc-module/src/config.rs:22` and `packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts`).
- Tool boundary hooks already exist: `createToolExecuteAfterHook` at `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/hook-handlers.ts:510`; `tool.execute.before/after` handled across `hook.ts`, `transform.ts`.
- No tool-latency instrumentation exists (no prefetch/speculative code found; `bd search` negative).
- `magic-context-9o6.3` plans a *pre-action* deterministic classifier on the same hook surface (warn-only interrupts). Different purpose (safety warnings vs latency hiding), shared plumbing.

## Desired State

Measure-first, flag-gated prototype. Two deliverables:

1. **Tool-latency instrumentation** (always on, cheap): record per-tool-signature wall time (tool name + coarse args class) into the session DB. Output: observed latency distribution so the prefetch threshold is data-backed, and so 9o6.3 can reuse it.
2. **Prefetch path** (config flag, default off):
   - On `tool.execute.before`, if the tool signature's expected duration exceeds a single threshold constant (start: 5s; no EV scheduler, no resource-class model), fire the existing recall/search path asynchronously with queries derived from tool args + active task context.
   - Hold results in a session-scoped buffer keyed by `(sessionId, callID)`, hard-capped (e.g. 4 entries, drop oldest). `ponytail:` fixed cap + drop-oldest; smarter eviction only if measurement demands it.
   - On `tool.execute.after` / next transform, deliver only fragments that pass the *existing* injection tiering and token budget. Unused entries dropped at turn end. Zero prompt change when flag off.
   - If retrieval hasn't completed by delivery time, skip silently (same discipline as 9o6.3).
3. **Metrics**: prefetch hit rate (prefetched fragment actually injected), recall latency saved on the turn path, wasted-work rate. Kill criterion: hit rate or latency savings too low → delete the flag and keep only the instrumentation.

**Simplicity gate:** reuse the existing recall entry points (`ctx_search` internals / injection pipeline); no new retrieval engine, no advisory types, no observation predicates. The only new mechanism is the trigger + bounded holding buffer.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/hook-handlers.ts` | latency capture at tool boundary; prefetch trigger | hooks already live here |
| `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/inject-compartments.ts` | accept pre-warmed results at delivery | reuse existing tiering/budget |
| `packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts` | flag + threshold | config twin discipline |
| session storage (`storage-db.ts` or session_meta) | latency rows | instrumentation |

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check ran on "tool-hook-triggered background retrieval with held results" — outcome: **place-adjacent**. `9o6.3` (planned, not implemented) is the only sibling; no existing prefetch/holding code. Implementing agent must coordinate trigger plumbing so 9o6.3 and this share one tool-signature classifier when both land.

### Blast Radius
Hook path latency is user-visible: the `tool.execute.before` work must be fire-and-forget (async task), never awaited on the hook path. Buffer lives in memory per session; bounded.

## Design Notes
Productionizing beyond the flag-gated prototype (buffer sizing under concurrency, cross-provider behavior, query-derivation quality) goes through `/plan-forge` with the measurement data from deliverable 1. This task intentionally stops at instrumented prototype + metrics. (design-risk gate: mechanism kept to bounded buffer + single threshold; envelope check deferred to plan-forge with real data.)

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| magic-context-9o6.3 | JIT memory interrupts on tool hooks | relates-to (shared trigger surface, different purpose) |
| magic-context-3q5.5 | Stage-decomposed benchmark harness | relates-to (measurement rides it) |
| magic-context-9o6 | Action-triggered memory epic | relates-to (same "action as trigger" thesis) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-tool-signature latency distribution recorded and queryable per session.
- [ ] Flag off ⇒ byte-identical prompt output (cache-parity baseline script unchanged).
- [ ] Flag on ⇒ no added blocking latency on the hook path (fire-and-forget verified).
- [ ] Delivered fragments pass existing injection budget/tiering; no new injection surface.
- [ ] Holding buffer hard-capped; entries dropped at turn end.
- [ ] Hit-rate / latency-saved / wasted-work metrics emitted.
- [ ] No new retrieval helper duplicating existing recall entry points.
- [ ] `cargo fmt && cargo check && cargo clippy` clean; bun tests pass.

## Pointers
- Brainstorm review (this session, 2026-08-22): rejected wider runtime; scope fence.
- `docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md` for perf measurement conventions.
- 9o6.3 description for the skip-silently/hard-budget discipline to mirror.

title: Applicability engine + retrieval-time read repair
description:
Feedback-adoption (2026-08 design review). Runtime half of U6c's applicability/anchor schema (magic-context-3q5.32). Recreated after dedup against main (was local U33/3q5.34).

## Goal
At retrieval time each candidate claim resolves to an applicability state against the caller's repo state; only `current` auto-injects; failed cheap checks repair the store instead of silently returning stale memory.

## Engine
- Reachability: is introduced_by/invalidated_by anchor reachable from current HEAD (git merge-base --is-ancestor; patch-id fallback for rebase/cherry-pick; tree/symbol-hash fallback when commits are gone).
- Dirty-tree overlap: uncommitted paths intersect affected_paths -> dirty_tree_uncertain.
- Cheap validity checks (read repair): referenced file exists, symbol still resolves, config key still present. Bounded per-query budget; results cached per (anchor, HEAD, dirty-fingerprint) generation — indexed point lookups in the spirit of R6, no per-candidate git subprocess spawns.
- On failure: mark stale/uncertain, append a verification_event (invalidation), schedule dreamer deep verification; never silently inject. Historical/uncertain stay reachable via explicit search, labeled.

## Interlocks
- Applicability is a hard lane filter beside trust (KTD19) for auto-inject; explicit search may include labeled historical results.
- Dreamer verify/map-memories remains the deep/batch layer; this unit is the cheap synchronous layer.
- Complements contradiction-first evidence bundles (magic-context-3q5.34): bundles show conflict/supersession, this shows repo-state applicability.
- R11 bounds apply: engine work is capped, cancellable, deadline-checked.

## Acceptance
- State-machine tests: current / historical / invalidated / dirty_tree_uncertain each discriminated by fixture repos; rebase and cherry-pick fixtures prove the patch-id fallback.
- Budget test: bounded and cancellable; zero git subprocess on cache hit.
- Read-repair oracle: a failed check writes an invalidation event and the same query stops auto-injecting the row without dreamer involvement.
close_reason: Absorbed into magic-context-kh8.5 (Scope algebra + anchor engine).

comments.author: AhravDutta
comments.text: U6c applicability contract landed at v85. Vocabulary contract: invalidation persists as state 'historical' plus a valid_until_anchor_id on a successor assertion — there is no 'invalidated' enum value (R4). Anchor resolution is strength-ordered (full commit OID > tree OID > stable patch ID); zero or multiple candidates at a level stay unresolved/ambiguous, patch IDs are never unique identity, and merge commits carry no patch representation yet. Evaluation streams require a checkout/environment context_fingerprint; a worktree-scoped evaluation must never publish a global project state.

title: Maturity ladder + taint promotion rules + visibility policy for claims
description:
Feedback-adoption (2026-08 design review). Policy half of the trust model; the trust-class/bitemporal COLUMNS land in U6c (magic-context-3q5.32) — this task consumes them. Recreated after dedup against main (was local U32/3q5.33).

## Goal
Claim lifecycle is an explicit maturity ladder with promotion rules and a visibility policy — repo prose can never become a durable directive; assistant inference can never silently become enforced policy.

## Model
- Taint labels (on U6c source trust class): USER_EXPLICIT, USER_INFERRED, CURRENT_CODE, CURRENT_TEST, CURRENT_CONFIG, REPO_UNTRUSTED_TEXT, TOOL_UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT, ASSISTANT_INFERENCE, DREAMER_INFERENCE.
- Promotion rules: REPO_UNTRUSTED_TEXT / TOOL_UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT may corroborate but never originate a directive-class claim; ASSISTANT/DREAMER inference caps below APPROVED without independent support or explicit user action.
- Maturity ladder distinct from archival status: CANDIDATE -> CORROBORATED -> VERIFIED -> APPROVED -> ENFORCED. Rejected / disputed / contradicted / stale / superseded stay separate epistemic states, not overloaded into one status field.
- Visibility matrix: auto-inject from VERIFIED+; CANDIDATE/CORROBORATED explicit-search only, labeled; ENFORCED points at an artifact (test/policy), not prose.

## Interlocks
- U8: trust_state on retrieval_documents derives from (taint, maturity); KTD19 lane eligibility consumes it.
- U18 (R16): contradicted/quarantined stay hard filters.
- U7 backfill mapping decided with U6c: dreamer-verified rows -> VERIFIED, others -> CORROBORATED (or better mapping with evidence).
- Anti-memory (9o6.1): a hard veto requires VERIFIED+.

## Acceptance
- Promotion-rule unit tests (repo text can never reach APPROVED without USER_EXPLICIT provenance or a verification event).
- Visibility policy is one table-driven function shared by auto-inject and explicit search.

title: Kernel-era retrieval epistemic metrics
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`.

## Goal
Measure whether retrieval returns canonically eligible, applicable evidence rather than only measuring rank quality.

## Metrics
- Canonical-ineligibility exposure: injected packets containing a candidate rejected at the query's `known_as_of`.
- Conflict surfacing: applicable asserted conflict, correction, or replacement relations shown with retrieved evidence.
- Stale-projection rejection: indexed candidates rejected because their source revision is no longer eligible.
- Abstention accuracy: no-memory and insufficient-evidence queries produce no hint or a typed empty result.
- Admission precision: sampled admitted propositions, decisions, observations, and evidence are useful and correctly scoped.

## Corpus
Add corrected decisions, branch-specific observations, deleted support, prompt-injection artifacts, and unknown-answer queries. Store fixture provenance and scope/anchor metadata.

## Reporting
Report these metrics beside Recall, MRR, nDCG, and latency for every benchmark run.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics and fixture categories are present in benchmark output; tests prove stale or ineligible candidates are not injected, conflicts are surfaced, and no-memory cases abstain.

title: Embedding input-token contract: derive limits from model card, fix MiniLM 512-vs-256
description:
Feedback-adoption (2026-08 design review). Standalone quick fix, ready now. Verified in code: packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-local.ts uses maxInputTokens = 512 while sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 declares max_seq_length 256 (its training distribution; maintainers state longer inputs degrade retrieval quality even though the transformer accepts them). 512-token compartment windows embed with a silently truncated/degraded tail.

## Goal
Chunk/window token budgets derive from the selected embedding model's actual retrieval contract, never a hard-coded constant.

## Changes
- Per-model contract table (input token limit, pooling, purpose prefixes) consulted by embedding-local and the chunker; MiniLM -> 256.
- Persist model+tokenizer version with every embedding (verify the R4/U8 eleven-field embedding-space identity already covers tokenizer version; wire if missing).
- Quality check at 64/128/256/512 lengths on the judged corpus to quantify the truncation effect (harness exists per U5).

## Interlocks
- U22 chunking and U24 embedding-space contract consume the same per-model table — do not duplicate it.
- KD5 unchanged: the default model stays MiniLM until the U26 gate; this only fixes the contract violation.

title: Kernel-era retrieval canaries
description:

## Scope

- Run canaries after embedding-model, tokenizer, text-view, chunking, ranking, projection, or schema changes.
- Include useful counterexample and non-applicability views.
- Keep canaries separate from human relevance labels.
- Include text-view version in embedding-space identity so changed views re-embed.

## Tests
Add a benchmark report section and an intentional regression proving that broken retrieval fails the canary.
acceptance_criteria: Canary pass is wired into the benchmark harness; fixtures use kernel identities and scope/anchor data; one intentional regression fails as expected.

title: Memory transmutation suggestions (dreamer task, suggestions-only)
description:
Knowledge should graduate out of prompt prose into stronger artifacts. New dreamer task scanning verified memories and proposing — never applying — a stronger representation:

- CONSTRAINTS / bug root cause -> proposed regression test
- PROJECT_RULES -> proposed CI/commit guard (suggestion text only, no generated enforcement)
- NAMING -> proposed lint rule
- ARCHITECTURE -> proposed ADR / doc section (extends existing maintain-docs task)
- Externalization pressure: "code/types now make this obvious — archive memory, keep searchable rationale pointer"

Surfaced like smart notes at natural boundaries. On acceptance, the memory shrinks to a compact pointer + artifact ref (test path, lint rule id, ADR link) — prompt budget shrinks while knowledge gets stronger.

Hard rule: LLM-extracted memories never auto-become enforcement. Suggestions only until acceptance-rate data justifies more.

## Measure

Suggestion acceptance rate; whether accepted artifacts later catch regressions; net prompt-token reduction from archived memories.

title: [epic] Action-triggered memory: anti-memory, failure signatures, JIT interrupts
description:
The differentiator line vs generic memory providers: surface prior rejections, failure lessons, and safety constraints at the moment the agent is about to repeat them — not as generic prompt injection. Three tasks, strictly sequenced: content types first (anti-memory, failure signatures), the action-hook surfacing layer last.

Guardrails for the whole line: warn-only (never block), hard per-turn budget, expiry/revalidation via dreamer so warnings don't calcify into stale institutional fear. Measured by repeated-rejected-approach rate, repeated-failure rate, and false-warning rate — a noisy interrupt system is worse than none.

title: Anti-memory: kernel-native rejected-approach records
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md` (R1, R4–R5, R7–R9). Kernel dependencies: `magic-context-kh8.2` and `magic-context-kh8.4`.

## Goal
Represent rejected approaches as typed kernel objects that produce scoped warnings when an agent is about to repeat a known failure.

## Record
Store immutable propositions for trigger and typed scope, rejected strategy, rejection reason and observed failure, preconditions and non-applicability, root cause, recovery, safer alternative, evidence references, and decision or observation links. Lifecycle, maturity, correction, replacement, expiry, and revalidation are separate append-only events.

## Admission and rendering
- Explicit user rejection may enter canonical state through deterministic admission.
- Extracted or retrospective candidates remain staging-only until admitted.
- Matching applicable records render as labeled warnings with a verification action.
- Nonmatching, stale, retracted, or unsupported records do not render.
- Records never render as neutral positive examples and never block execution.
design: Register a rejected-approach object kind. Store fields as immutable propositions, evidence as asserted edges, and maturity or validity as lifecycle events.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit rejection creates a scoped canonical record with evidence; staged candidates stay invisible; matching preconditions warn with a verification action; nonmatching records do not warn; correction is append-only; evidence deletion removes automatic visibility; rejected approaches never render as positive guidance; repeat rate, false-warning rate, and token overhead are measurable.
notes: Warn-only behavior is invariant. Procedure execution and hard blocking remain excluded.

## Scope

title: Smart-note evaluator: due-check backlog can starve compilation
description:
select_next_smart_note_evaluation (crates/mc-module/src/smart_note_evaluation.rs) applies strict phase priority (due > compile > liveness > fallback) per claim acquisition. A project with >= MAX_CLAIMS_PER_DRAIN (25) recurring due checks per timer tick consumes every drain iteration with 'due' claims, so notes needing compilation are never selected and stay uncompiled indefinitely despite a healthy evaluator. Raised by codex review on PR #12 (comment 3815004109).

Fix needs a fairness-policy design decision, not a mechanical patch: the selection function is a stateless pure function per acquisition (no drain-scoped state on the Rust side), and its semantics are pinned by the frozen characterization fixture smart-note-evaluation-golden.json (regeneration diff = semantic change requiring review, per PARITY.md). Candidate shapes: (a) per-phase quotas tracked drain-side via a phase hint in the claim request, (b) aging promotion using a 'needs compile since' timestamp (new snapshot/store field), (c) deterministic interleave. Whichever is chosen must update the golden/normative fixtures and PARITY.md.

comments.author: AhravDutta
comments.text: Second starvation case from claude review (PR #12 comment 3815629689): get_fallback_smart_notes has no attempt gate and deterministic input order, so a note whose fallback confirmation keeps returning false is re-selected first on every drain and later fallback notes never get a confirmation. The worker's per-drain dedup + break bounds the billable loop but cannot reach note 2 (releasing the claim just hands note 1 back). The same fairness redesign should add a re-selection gate (e.g. last_checked_at spacing) to fallback selection alongside the per-phase quota work.

title: Fence module evaluator claim selection by checkout root
description: PR #12 review follow-up (codex 3814664230, claude 3814681244, claude 3814682201): two checkouts/worktrees sharing a root-commit project identity draw from one project-wide pending set, while each worker's filesystem capabilities bind to its own checkout root — so a file-dependent note can be compiled/evaluated against the wrong checkout. Three surfaces share the gap: (1) claim selection carries no originating route root; (2) the dream-timer drain falls back to any same-identity bridge when the exact (identity, root) bridge is missing (deliberate: an undrained module queue is worse, but it widens the wrong-root window); (3) the noteEvaluationAvailable write gate is identity-scoped, consistent with the current model but should tighten to exact-root once claims are fenced. This matches legacy sweep semantics (each registration's sweep evaluated the shared identity-scoped note set against its own root). A real fix persists the originating route root per note (or per claim) and fences claim selection to the worker's route — a store schema + protocol change, out of scope for PR #12.

title: F7 redact handler panic payloads from stderr
description: Finding: Handler panic payloads escape to process stderr. Severity SHOULD FIX (P1), security. Files: mc-host runtime/dispatch panic boundary, public runtime contract, and subprocess tests. Tokio JoinError maps a handler panic to a redacted wire error only after Rust's global panic hook prints the original payload; a nocapture run prints CANARY-BODY-51ab. Establish explicit panic-hook ownership for mc-host callback tasks: host callback panics must emit only a fixed redacted diagnostic while unrelated process panics still reach the prior hook. Since hooks are process-global, design scoped/thread-local callback marking and serialized installation/restoration or a documented single-install runtime policy that remains sound under concurrent hosts. First add a subprocess stderr test that fails on the canary, confirm failure, implement minimally, then run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Handler callback panic bodies never appear on stderr or wire; stderr contains only a fixed redacted host diagnostic; unrelated panics still chain to the previous hook; subprocess coverage verifies policy without contaminating the test process; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Resolved and verified P1 wave: host-reserved OutputBuffer enforces pre-allocation egress accounting with deterministic concurrent coverage; registry atomically registers dispatch tasks with route liveness and close ownership; callback-poll panic hook redacts handler payloads while chaining unrelated panics. Full mc-host tests and strict lib/test clippy pass; all-target clippy is blocked only by unrelated untracked perf_load.rs.

title: F6 make dispatch registration atomic with route close
description: Finding: Route close can overtake dispatch registration. Severity SHOULD FIX (P1), concurrency correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/routing.rs, dispatch.rs, connection.rs and routing/dispatch/lifecycle tests. dispatch_request obtains route_cancel while Live, then spawns/inserts pending state and only later register_task; close may take the task list, run route_gone, and queue Goodbye before the admitted request's cancellation terminal. Add one registry-owned dispatch reservation atomically while Live and make close account for every reservation/task before route-gone/Goodbye. Inspect existing race loops and extend them; create a deterministic failing barrier-based test, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: No admitted routed request can register or emit after route close has drained and route_gone has run; close joins/settles every atomic dispatch reservation; a deterministic race test proves terminal-before-Goodbye ordering and zero post-close handler activity; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Resolved and verified P1 wave: host-reserved OutputBuffer enforces pre-allocation egress accounting with deterministic concurrent coverage; registry atomically registers dispatch tasks with route liveness and close ownership; callback-poll panic hook redacts handler payloads while chaining unrelated panics. Full mc-host tests and strict lib/test clippy pass; all-target clippy is blocked only by unrelated untracked perf_load.rs.

title: F3 reserve handler output memory before allocation
description: Finding: Handler responses bypass resident-memory budget. Severity SHOULD FIX (P1), performance/correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/handler.rs, dispatch.rs, runtime.rs/config.rs and dispatch tests. A handler currently returns an already allocated Vec and only afterward does emit_frame charge egress, allowing up to max_handler_tasks times MAX_BODY_LEN outside max_resident_bytes. Redesign the handler-facing response/stream allocation contract so host egress capacity is reserved before handler-controlled body allocation and the reservation is carried through enqueue without double charging. First inspect existing dispatch memory tests and extend the narrowest existing form; add a deterministic failing concurrent accounting test, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Handler unary responses and stream items cannot allocate host-accounted output beyond reserved egress capacity before a charge exists; reservations transfer to writer ownership exactly once and release on all errors/cancellation; deterministic tests cover concurrency and cleanup; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Resolved and verified P1 wave: host-reserved OutputBuffer enforces pre-allocation egress accounting with deterministic concurrent coverage; registry atomically registers dispatch tasks with route liveness and close ownership; callback-poll panic hook redacts handler payloads while chaining unrelated panics. Full mc-host tests and strict lib/test clippy pass; all-target clippy is blocked only by unrelated untracked perf_load.rs.

description: Finding: Host uses private protocol versions instead of published authority. Severity SHOULD FIX (P1), dependency correctness/security. title: Daemon reranker cascade for explicit search
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`.

## Goal
Provide an optional daemon-hosted quality lift for explicit search without adding reranker latency to automatic search.

## Scope
- Keep the reranker disabled by default until benchmarks show positive lift within the global p95 gate.
- Stage one uses bounded contiguous features from lexical rank, dense rank, exact match, source kind, canonical eligibility, scope applicability, freshness, support relations, and duplication.
- Stage two runs a cross-encoder only for candidates with overlapping score intervals.
- Enforce pair and total-token caps before dispatch, then apply a hard deadline.
- On deadline expiry, return stage-one ordering.
- Automatic search never invokes this reranker.

## Tests
Cover zero encoder calls for separated candidates, encoder use for uncertainty sets, pre-dispatch pair/token caps, deadline behavior, missing-lane features without NaNs, and disabled-mode identity with fusion and packing output.
design: Eligibility validation precedes feature extraction. Stage two may reorder only the bounded uncertainty set.
acceptance_criteria: Reranker stays disabled unless measured lift is positive and p95 remains acceptable; auto-search never invokes it; all work caps and deadline tests pass.

title: U19: Dedup + token-budget packing
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (U5 gate reaches this unit through its U18 dependency): benchmark duplicate-rate and tokens-per-useful-result must improve vs baseline. Note: U18's fusion-parity success criterion is measured on THIS unit's packed output.

## Goal
Delivered context maximizes usefulness per token.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R20: "Final packing deduplicates exact and near-duplicate results (preserving independent provenance as cluster metadata), merges overlapping ordinal intervals, and selects under a token budget by marginal utility per token."

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/result-packing.ts (+ test)
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-search/tools.ts

## Approach
1. Collapse exact normalized hashes; SimHash/MinHash near-duplicate clusters with provenance preserved as cluster metadata; merge overlapping session ordinal intervals.
2. Greedy/CELF selection under the token budget; coverage of query atoms/claims/episodes/artifacts as bitsets so marginal gain is AND-NOT + POPCNT-style cheap.

## Test scenarios
- Two near-identical memories (one-word diff) form one cluster; output carries both provenances once.
- Overlapping compartment/message intervals merge; non-overlapping stay distinct.
- A budget of N tokens is NEVER exceeded (property test over random result sets); a higher-marginal-utility item displaces a duplicative higher-scored item.
- Empty results and single-result inputs pass through unchanged.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark duplicate-rate and tokens-per-useful-result improve vs baseline.
notes:
judge-ruling: U5 gate reaches this unit transitively via U18 - direct edge intentionally omitted per adjudication (minimal graph, gate obligation carried in description); reduce-complexity: bitset coverage keeps marginal-gain computation cheap - perf-first shape; less-code: minimal; ponytail-review: SimHash/MinHash scoped to near-dup clustering only; invariant-test-review: budget cap proven as a PROPERTY over random result sets, displacement oracle discriminates utility-vs-score; test-strategy: property test for the budget invariant + examples for cluster/merge edges
DELTA (future-enhancements review): packing objective gains a facet-coverage term — at least one item per unresolved query facet from the U16 query AST; penalize near-duplicates that answer the same facet. Prevents five similar memories all answering one part of a three-part question. Benchmark-gated under U5.

title: search.sqlite lexical lanes and identifier indexes
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`.

## Goal
Build daemon-owned prose and identifier retrieval lanes over admitted retrieval documents in `search.sqlite`.

## Scope
- Use FTS5 for prose and dedicated indexes for paths, symbols, object identifiers, commit SHAs, error codes, and supported short needles.
- Consume only projector output from admitted canonical state.
- Use the daemon query AST for all lexical lanes.
- Publish rebuilt indexes atomically and keep projector checkpoints consistent with indexed content.
- Replace repeated tokenization and `shift()` copying with index-based linear splitting and memoized token counts while preserving byte-identical chunks and separator hierarchy.
- Keep retrieval counters such as seen count, retrieval count, and last-retrieved time outside FTS-triggered document rows so counter updates never rebuild FTS content.
- Emit deterministic counters for splitter operations/copies, split count, planned lexical subqueries, capped or dropped atoms, lane executions, rows examined, and FTS-trigger activity.
- Remove alternate lexical query paths once this lane is active.

## Tests
Cover byte-identical splitter goldens, separator fallback behavior, a linear operation-count oracle on 1 MB input, prose, paths, symbols, SHAs, short needles, bounded splitting, counter accounting, counter updates with zero FTS-trigger work, concurrent projection, atomic rebuild publication, and absence of alternate production lexical paths.
acceptance_criteria: search.sqlite lanes are the only production lexical path; splitter output remains byte-identical; operation counters prove linear scaling; retrieval-counter updates do not touch FTS rows; bounded-work counters and the benchmark gate pass.

title: U18: Global weighted RRF cutover + progressive deepening
description:
Phase 4. Benchmark-gated global weighted RRF.

## Goal
Make weighted reciprocal-rank fusion the only cross-source ranking path.

## Rules
- No RRF feature flag.
- No flag-off legacy ranking.
- No byte-identical legacy-ranking requirement.
- Benchmark comparison happens before merge on a fixture baseline, not at runtime.
- New sources enter the same fusion contract immediately.

## Approach
1. Apply trust and conflict eligibility before ranks enter fusion.
2. Use one global RRF formula with versioned lane weights.
3. Deepen lanes only while unseen candidates can still beat the current result boundary.
4. Delete cosine/BM25 arithmetic mixing, static source boosts, and old scoring code.
5. Keep only bounded error handling. A failed new engine call fails closed or returns a typed error; it does not select the old ranker.

## Test scenarios
- Fused metrics meet U5 thresholds on final packed output.
- Excluded candidates never affect ranks.
- Progressive deepening stops only when its bound proves safe.
- Every search call uses the new ranker.

## Verification
- No runtime configuration selects the old ranker.
- Old scoring modules and flag-off tests are deleted.
acceptance_criteria: No runtime flag selects old scoring; U5 benchmark passes; old ranker and flag-off tests are deleted.
notes: Removed RRF flag-off compatibility. New weighted RRF is the only ranker in the supported release.

title: Daemon query analyzer and cost-based retrieval planner
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`.

## Goal
Run one deterministic query analyzer and planner inside the daemon over kernel-era retrieval indexes.

## Scope
- Use one maximal-munch lexer and typed AST for object identifiers, proposition or decision identifiers, commit SHAs, paths, symbols, error codes, quoted phrases, temporal terms, and prose.
- Reuse the AST for exact lookup, FTS5 formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion, and packing coverage.
- Enforce query-atom and work caps before planning.
- Resolve exact identifiers without embedding.
- Run lexical-first or lexical-only plans when confidence permits; run mixed lanes when needed.
- Maintain document-frequency data during projection. A Count-Min Sketch is allowed only where overestimation can only downweight work.
- Support typed abstention when post-eligibility evidence is insufficient.

## Tests
Retain lexer goldens, zero-embedding exact-ID tests, rare-versus-ambiguous planning tests, frequency add/remove tests, safe-overestimation properties, empty-query behavior, and abstention fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Analyzer and planner run daemon-side; work caps precede dispatch; exact identifiers make no embedding call; lexical-heavy benchmark categories remain within the global regression gate.

title: U15: Benchmark-gated layout/cascade/batching variants
description:
Phase 3. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; every variant here lands ONLY on a measured win vs the U10 baseline (R28). Success-criteria coupling: the 128 MB decoded-index target is CONTINGENT on a U15 compressed variant winning its recall gate; if none passes, the memory threshold relaxes to the f32 baseline (~154 MB) and R12's ANN trigger fires (ANN itself stays deferred/trigger-gated — no HNSW work here).

## Goal
Measure the hardware bets; adopt only winners.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: "Hardware-level bets (AoSoA layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades, GEMM micro-batching, mmap layouts) land only on measured wins against the row-major f32 exact baseline with stable tie-breaking, reporting recall and ranking quality for every approximate variant."
- KTD10: "AoSoA block-transposed layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades (conservative Cauchy-Schwarz pruning: skip when prefix_dot + query_tail_norm x candidate_tail_norm < kth_score, tail norms stored per candidate), and GEMM-style micro-batching of concurrent queries are benchmark-gated variants behind the same trait."
- Plan risk note (small-K reality check): "Top-K specialization and micro-batching pay off only under load; U12/U15 measure before adopting."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (variant modules + benches)

## Approach
Implement behind the VectorIndex trait and bench against the row-major exact baseline across the U5 matrix:
(a) AoSoA block-transposed layout;
(b) int8/f16 and Matryoshka-prefix cascade with tail-norm Cauchy-Schwarz pruning and oversampled full-f32 rerank;
(c) GEMM-style micro-batching for concurrent same-generation queries with a scheduler choosing shard-one-query / independent / batch (no added latency for isolated interactive queries).
Adopt per measured win; document losers and REMOVE their code (dead variants do not ship).

## Test scenarios
- Cascade preserves EXACT top-K on the comparator corpus when exact-mode pruning is enabled (tolerance-aware float handling asserted).
- Quantized recall reported per configuration; any recall < 1.0 variant is marked approximate and EXCLUDED from exact mode.
- Batching: 4 concurrent queries on one generation read vector pages once (bytes-touched counter) and match serial results.

## Verification
- Bench report vs the U10 baseline committed; only winning variants remain enabled.
notes: reduce-complexity: three bets behind the existing trait, no new seams; less-code: losers deleted, not flag-parked (plan-mandated); perf: this unit IS the measured-perf discipline (R28); ponytail-review: micro-batching pays only under load - measured before adopting per plan risk note; invariant-test-review: exact-mode cascade oracle = exact top-K preservation with tolerance-aware float compare, approximate variants must report recall and are excluded from exact mode; test-strategy: comparator property + bytes-touched counters + bench-gated adoption

title: Daemon retrieval routes, authorization, queues, and cancellation
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`. Kernel route dependency: `magic-context-kh8.8`.

## Goal
Expose lexical and dense retrieval through daemon-native routes with bounded work, server-derived authorization, cancellation, and reserved interactive capacity.

## Scope
- Accept query text or vectors, normalized filters, K, embedding-space identity, and deadlines.
- Derive authorized scope and visibility server-side, then intersect requested filters with that authority.
- Include authorized scope, normalized filters, embedding space, index generation, and canonical revision in singleflight and cache keys.
- Keep inference, normalization, scan, top-K, eligibility validation, and result hydration daemon-side.
- Use bounded interactive and background queues. Background work cannot consume reserved interactive capacity.
- Route native and thin-client search through the same engine.
- Return typed unavailability when the daemon is down. A cold dense lane may use daemon lexical retrieval; it never invokes a client-side search implementation.

## Tests
Cover scope isolation under colliding query hashes, widened filters, cancellation between scan blocks, same-scope singleflight, queue saturation, cold-index behavior, and daemon-unavailable behavior.
design: Coalescing keys bind authorization and complete retrieval state, not query text alone.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization cannot be widened by request filters or cache sharing; work and queues are bounded; cancellation works; interactive capacity remains available; daemon loss returns typed unavailability.

title: Vector segment persistence and daemon outbox projector
description:
Authority: `docs/plans/2026-08-29-2016-refactor-semantic-kernel-beads-restructure-plan.md`. Kernel outbox dependency: `magic-context-kh8.2`.

## Goal
Let the daemon consume canonical outbox events and write crash-safe vector segments and manifests directly under `vectors/`.

## Scope
- Use immutable base and bounded delta segments with tombstones.
- Publish generations by writing and syncing segments, validating them, then atomically replacing the manifest.
- Pin generations for active readers and retire old generations only after readers drain.
- Consume outbox events idempotently and advance durable projector checkpoints.
- Compact segments without changing live search results.
- Enforce byte-bounded residency by project and embedding space with LRU eviction.
- Expose projector lag and prevent stale projected candidates from reaching injection through canonical eligibility validation.

## Tests
A crash between segment sync and manifest publication reopens the old generation intact; compaction equals the prior result set minus deletions; pinned readers finish on their generation; redelivery produces one logical vector effect; eviction and reload preserve results.
design: Daemon projector owns both outbox consumption and vector manifest state. Manifest publication is the only visibility boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Crash, compaction, redelivery, generation-pinning, checkpoint, and eviction tests pass; no client-initiated vector ingestion protocol remains.

title: U12: Kernel dispatch + top-K selection benchmarks
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Runtime-dispatched kernels and a measured top-K structure choice.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: measure, do not assume — variants land only on measured wins.
- KTD2: safe-SIMD-first with "runtime-dispatched NEON and AVX2/FMA variants (AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed) and no blanket target-cpu=native".

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/kernels.rs, src/topk.rs, benches/

## Approach
1. Kernel set: portable scalar, NEON (+dot-product extension where present), AVX2/FMA; feature-detected dispatch at index-open; no target-cpu=native artifacts.
2. Top-K candidates: fixed-capacity sorted array, binary heap, buffered select_nth_unstable — benched at K in {5, 32, 100}; the winner per K-band becomes the default. Losing structures do not ship as dead code (global Definition of Done: no dead experiment code).
3. Consecutive-window group max: retain max while walking (compartment_id, window_index) order instead of map+sort.

## Test scenarios
- All kernels agree with scalar EXACTLY (shared comparator harness from U10).
- Dispatch on a host lacking a feature falls back cleanly (force-disable flag in tests).
- Top-K structures agree with a full-sort reference across K values and duplicate scores.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench table (kernel x dims, structure x K) in the PR.
notes: reduce-complexity: ok; less-code: losing top-K structures REMOVED after measurement, only the winner ships (no dead experiment code); perf: measured K-band selection is the whole point; ponytail-review: AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed (KTD2), nothing speculative built; invariant-test-review: exact-agreement oracle vs scalar comparator including duplicate-score ties, force-disable fallback test; test-strategy: comparator property harness reused from U10 + bench table

title: U10: mc-vector crate: exact engine + trait
description:
Phase 3 — Rust dense engine. Develops in parallel with Phase 2 against synthetic corpora; integration comes in U13. Ships no ranking change itself, but its criterion baseline is the R28 correctness comparator that U15 measures against.

## Goal
The ID-first exact engine exists as a standalone crate with the VectorIndex abstraction.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R9: "Hot-path dense search runs in Rust over contiguous normalized vectors and returns compact (ordinal, score) pairs; stable IDs, text, and metadata hydrate only after fusion selects final candidates."
- R12: "Exact search is the default engine. ANN (HNSW) is added only behind the VectorIndex abstraction when measured thresholds are crossed: auto-search p95 above ~25 ms or active decoded index above ~128 MB for a scope." This unit lands the abstraction SEAM only — no HNSW work.
- R14: in-memory generation shape (immutable generation + tombstones).
- KTD1: "Dense engine lives in a new crates/mc-vector crate, exposed as routes on the existing ck-mc module ... mc-vector depends only on workspace-internal crates (no subc/cortexkit deps) so it builds and benches in isolation."
- KTD2: "Safe-SIMD-first kernels with runtime dispatch. The workspace is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] everywhere; mc-vector starts with a safe SIMD abstraction (pulp or wide) over a portable scalar baseline ... Unsafe is admitted only if benchmarks prove the safe abstraction leaves large wins on the table."
- KTD3: "Shard-local top-K per worker, merge workers x K; cancellation checked between scan blocks; never a shared heap in the scan loop."
- KTD10: "Row-major f32 exact scan is the baseline and correctness comparator."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (new: src/lib.rs, src/generation.rs, src/scan.rs, src/topk.rs, src/scratch.rs, criterion benches under benches/)
- root Cargo.toml workspace member

## Approach
1. Generation structure: packed normalized f32 row-major matrix, stable_ids: Vec<u64> (cold), filter bitmaps, tombstone bitset, group ranges (compartment -> ordinal range), generation id. QueryScratch with scores, seen-epoch, touched list, fixed-capacity top-K.
2. Dense u32 ordinals internally; (ordinal, score) output; stable-ID conversion only after top-K.
3. Normalize on index, normalize query once, dot product only; shard-local top-K, merge workers x K on a dedicated compute pool (KTD3).
4. VectorIndex trait: search(partition, query, k, filters, deadline), build_generation(docs), publish_generation(gen); ExactIndex is the first impl.
5. Scalar reference implementation kept as the correctness comparator; safe-SIMD kernels via pulp/wide (KTD2).
Directional: exact top-K with stable tie-breaking (score desc, ordinal asc).

## Test scenarios
- Property-test comparison: random corpus (1k x {128,384,1024}), random queries — SIMD scan top-K equals the scalar reference EXACTLY under stable tie-breaking, with and without tombstones.
- Deleted (tombstoned) ordinals never appear in results.
- K > live corpus returns all live, sorted.
- Deadline expiring mid-scan returns a cancelled error, NOT partial results presented as complete.
- Zero-vector and duplicate-vector inputs behave (no NaN; duplicates tie-break by ordinal).
- cargo bench baseline recorded for the scan across the U5 matrix dims.

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; criterion baseline committed as a snapshot for U15 comparisons.
notes: reduce-complexity: VectorIndex trait seam is R12-mandated for future ANN, not speculative; less-code: scalar reference doubles as the correctness comparator - not dead code; perf: criterion baseline IS a deliverable (R28 comparator); ponytail-review: no HNSW, no unsafe - both trigger-gated per plan; invariant-test-review: SIMD-vs-scalar exact-equality property oracle under stable tie-breaking, deadline test asserts cancelled error rather than silent partials; test-strategy: property-based comparator + example edge cases (zero-vector, duplicates, K over corpus)

title: U11: Bitmap filters + adaptive scan
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Filters cut memory traffic, not just results.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R10: "Filtering (project, session, source type, trust, status, embedding space, time/ordinal range) uses bitmaps applied before or inside the scan so excluded vectors never touch the memory hierarchy; the scan strategy adapts to filter selectivity (dense masked scan, sparse gather, or segment skip)."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/filter.rs (new), src/scan.rs

## Approach
1. Bitmaps per project/session/source/trust/status/space + coarse ordinal/time ranges; raw bitsets for dense sets, Roaring-style containers for sparse; the crossover is MEASURED per architecture (bench, not assumed).
2. Strategy selection by allowed-set density: dense -> sequential masked scan; sparse -> set-bit enumeration + gather; range-restricted -> whole-segment skip via min/max metadata.

## Test scenarios
- Each strategy returns IDENTICAL results to the reference filter-then-scan for random filter sets at 0.1% / 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% selectivity.
- Segment-skip: a query restricted to an ordinal range touches only overlapping segments (assert via scan counters).
- Empty filter set returns empty WITHOUT touching vectors.
- Bench records bytes-touched per selectivity point — proves the R10 mechanism (excluded vectors are not read), not just output correctness.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench comparison in PR notes.

title: U9: Verify direct cutover and remove legacy surfaces
description:
Phase 2. Direct claims cutover verification and legacy-surface removal.

## Goal
Prove that the direct cutover is complete and remove any remaining compatibility surface. This is not a delayed reader migration. U7 and U8 already use claims and the claims-native retrieval projection.

## Scope
- Re-point search, mural, dreamer, module state-sync, dashboard/TUI, and native module routes to claim current-state and retrieval documents.
- Remove mutable semantic `memories` reads and writes, compatibility crosswalks, backfill runners, old embedding tables, and compatibility-only schema guards.
- Remove legacy result-ID adapters, old memory-shaped wire payloads, and compatibility feature flags.
- Keep only fail-closed schema-version checks and correctness-preserving atomic index staging. Do not preserve an old implementation for rollback.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh fixture outputs match the claims-native expected results.
- Search, mural, dreamer, module, dashboard, and Pi/OpenCode paths contain no legacy fallback.
- Static reference scan finds no production import of compatibility modules.
- Direct writes to removed legacy tables fail because the tables do not exist.
- Unsupported old databases fail closed with an actionable reset message.

## Verification
- Full bun, cargo, plugin, Pi, CLI, dashboard, and e2e suites pass.
- The final schema and dependency graph contain one semantic write/read approach.
acceptance_criteria: All readers and wire/dashboard paths use claims; compatibility modules, tables, flags, and old payloads are removed; fresh-schema and static reference checks pass.
notes: This is cleanup and verification, not a delayed coexistence phase. U7 and U8 must already be claims-native.

## Goal

## Scope

## Tests
Redelivery produces one logical effect; a fresh canonical mutation projects once; rebuilds produce identical identities, hashes, postings, and checkpoints; duplicate content shares storage within one embedding space; staging is absent; derived-store corruption does not alter canonical state.

title: U7: Direct claims cutover for memory storage
description:
Phase 2. Direct claims cutover for memory storage.

## Goal
Claims become the only semantic source of truth. All memory writers and readers use the claims/revision/evidence API from their first supported release.

There are no legacy callers, deployed users, or existing databases to preserve. Do not implement memories-to-claims backfill, dual-read, a maintained `memories` compatibility projection, legacy IDs, or a later reader migration.

## Scope
- Make claims/revisions/evidence the storage API for OpenCode, Pi, dreamer, historian, module mirror, dashboard, identity merge, relocation, verification, and session paths.
- Use operation envelopes for retries and request-key reuse detection.
- Commit claim revisions, evidence, lifecycle state, outbox effects, and generations atomically.
- Replace mutable memory IDs with canonical claim/revision/retrieval-document identities at API boundaries.
- Update the module wire and dashboard/TUI payloads to new claim-native shapes in this cutover.
- Delete `legacy_memory_claims`, `claim_backfill_*`, `hasMemoryClaimsCompatSchema`, `storage-memory-projection.ts`, and compatibility-only guards and startup runners.
- Treat old `context.db` files and old binaries as unsupported. Reset or refuse them; do not migrate them.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/context-authority.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/relocate-memory.ts
- packages/pi-plugin/src/tools/ctx-memory.ts
- packages/cli/src/commands/doctor*.ts

## Test scenarios
- Every semantic write creates or appends claim state with one atomic commit.
- Every reader uses claim current-state and evidence.
- A fresh database has no mutable semantic `memories` source.
- No production SQL path reads or writes compatibility tables.
- Crash injection proves no partial claim/evidence/outbox/generation commit.
- Replayed operations return the stored result without duplicate effects.
- Unsupported old databases fail closed.

## Verification
- Full plugin, Pi, CLI, dashboard, and e2e suites pass on fresh databases.
- Static search finds no legacy memory compatibility branch or reader.
design: Implement the claims-only greenfield cutover. Rewire every writer, reader, wire boundary, and dashboard path together; remove memories compatibility tables, backfill, dual-read branches, and old IDs. Preserve only atomicity, replay safety, and fail-closed fences.
acceptance_criteria: All writers and readers use claims-native APIs; no compatibility tables or backfill runner; fresh database has no mutable semantic memories source; crash and replay tests pass; unsupported old DBs fail closed.
notes: Supersedes dual-read/backfill design. User confirmed greenfield conditions: no legacy callers, deployed users, or existing databases. Claims-only cutover is required.

title: U6: Claims/evidence authoritative schema
description:
Phase 2. Claims and evidence domain.

## Goal
Make claims, revisions, evidence, conflicts, and verification events the only semantic storage contract for fresh databases.

This is a greenfield cutover. There are no supported legacy callers, deployed users, or legacy databases to migrate. Do not add a compatibility projection, dual-read API, or memory-row backfill.

## Scope
- Create the authoritative claims/evidence schema and numeric project identity registry.
- Enforce immutable revisions, evidence links, current-revision CAS, project ownership, and fail-closed corruption reads.
- Expose transaction-local writers and current-state readers for every new caller.
- Reject unsupported old schema versions and old binaries. Refusal is a safety fence, not a compatibility contract.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/storage-claims-schema.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- migration and schema-fence tests

## Approach
1. Build the claims schema for the new database shape.
2. Make claims/revisions/evidence writes atomic and append-only.
3. Do not seed claims from `memories`; fresh fixtures create claims directly.
4. Remove assumptions that a mutable memory row is authoritative.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh database creates only the new semantic schema.
- Claim creation and revision append preserve prior bytes.
- Stale current-revision writes roll back without partial rows.
- Direct SQL corruption is detected or rejected.
- Unsupported old schema versions fail closed.

## Verification
- Claims schema, migration, fence, and corruption tests pass.
- No production caller reads or writes legacy memory state.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh claims schema and project registry; immutable revision/evidence/CAS tests pass; unsupported old schemas fail closed; no production caller reads or writes legacy memory state.
notes: Greenfield decision: claims are the only semantic source. No legacy memory rows, compatibility projection, dual-read, or backfill. Old schema and old binaries fail closed.

title: Decide whether an UPDATE verdict should carry VERIFIED maturity to the revision it creates
description:
## Observation

`stageVerificationItem`'s UPDATE branch records `outcome: "update"` against the
OLD revision, then creates the corrected revision (and, since b4f6908e, a TTL
renewal revision). Neither new revision receives a verification event:

    packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/dreamer/verify.ts (update branch)

`autoEligible` requires `MATURITY_RANK[maturity] >= MATURITY_RANK.VERIFIED`
(`claim-visibility-policy.ts:185-196`), and the revised content carries dreamer
`model_inference` provenance. So immediately after an UPDATE the corrected
warning stops being eligible for automatic delivery, while remaining available
to explicit search with a label.

Raised by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #78 (P2), which reads this as a defect:
UPDATE is the verifier's positive replacement verdict, so the replacement should
inherit its maturity.

## The competing reading

The content after an UPDATE is model-authored. The VERIFIED+ gate on automatic
surfaces exists precisely so a model-authored assertion is not injected into a
user's prompt without corroboration — the same rule the anti-memory lane
enforces when it rejects `!item.policy.autoEligible`. On that reading, an
UPDATE demoting a warning out of automatic delivery is the gate working, not
failing.

The demotion is also self-healing rather than permanent: the revised claim is
not `stale`, so it stays in `partitionVerifyScope`'s candidate set, and
`verifiedAt()` returns 0 for it, which puts it in the next incremental
verification batch.

## Decision needed

Either:

- an UPDATE records `verified` against the final revision, making the verifier's
  replacement verdict authoritative for maturity; or
- the current behaviour is documented at the UPDATE branch as deliberate, naming
  the one-cycle automatic-delivery gap and why model-authored replacement text
  must be re-corroborated.

Whichever is chosen, a test should assert the maturity of the revision an UPDATE
leaves behind, since today nothing pins it.

title: Validate input-lock identity in production selection once U9 qualifies payloads
description:
`generation_identity_matches` compares `target` and
`release_contract_sha256` but not `inputs_lock_sha256`, so a generation staged by
`start --payload-dir` — whose manifest records the marker
`inputs_lock_sha256: "unqualified-dev-inputs"` — is accepted by a later plain
`start` or `restart`.

That reuse is currently intended and asserted. `lifecycle_cli`'s
`full_dev_mode_lifecycle_roundtrip` runs a bare `restart` after dev staging and
requires it to succeed:

    // restart from stopped: no --payload-dir needed, the promoted current
    // generation revalidates; stop bit stays false.

And because U9 records `production_qualified:false`, no supported flow can stage
a qualified payload today — so rejecting unqualified generations in production
selection would make the entire non-`--payload-dir` path fail universally rather
than fail closed on a specific hazard.

Once U9 flips `production_qualified` to true and a qualified payload can exist,
an input-lock identity comparison becomes meaningful and should be added to
`generation_identity_matches` alongside the target and release-contract checks,
with the dev marker rejected on the production path.

Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #49 (comment 3875686005), declined
there with this reasoning.

title: Decide the fate of the repo-wide 'commentlint: allow(JUDGE)' comment marker

comments). It predates the current work by many commits and is referenced by
no script, config, or documentation in the tree.

CodeRabbit flagged the single occurrence inside PR #49's diff
(crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs:3026) as an unrecognized lint directive that
resembles an attempt to suppress an automated reviewer, and asked for it to be
removed and its origin investigated.

It is a pre-existing convention, not something PR #49 introduced, so removing
one occurrence would only make the tree inconsistent. Two coherent options:

1. Keep it and document what consumes it, so future reviewers can tell it is
   deliberate rather than an injection attempt.
2. Retire it in one sweep across all 52 files.

Either way it is a repo-wide decision, not a change that belongs in a PR about
the native daemon lifecycle runtime.

title: Retain skipped frames in RawClient::frames_until_corr
description:
The test support helper `RawClient::frames_until_corr` returns the frames it consumed while searching, but most call sites discard them with `let (_, response) = ...`. Those frames are the only copy, so a later sequential call for a correlation whose response was already consumed waits out its whole budget.

This produced one real flake, fixed in 29e6f4a1 by having `pipelined_shutdown_requests_on_one_connection_both_settle` read the second response out of the returned list. The remaining exposure is latent: a stray bootstrap `Ping` gets skipped during TCP negotiation, which is harmless because `frames_until_corr` already excludes `TY_PING` from matching and no test asserts on the resulting Pong.

The durable fix is to stop discarding the skipped frames — buffer them on the client so a later `frames_until_corr` searches the buffer before reading the socket — and audit every call site together rather than adding local exceptions. Doing that per-site is what allowed one flake to exist already.
acceptance_criteria: Consumed non-matching frames are buffered and reachable by a later search; every frames_until_corr call site audited; the pipelined-shutdown test still passes without its local lookaside.

title: Extract shared PID start-time probes for reuse by the Rust e2e reaper
description:
packages/e2e-tests/src/rust-runner/hermetic-mc-host.ts has processStartTimeMs and processExecutable for leak reaping, which overlap with packages/plugin/src/shared/rpc-utils.ts.

The overlap is not directly reusable as it stands. isPidIdentityPlausible takes an RpcPortFileRecord and its legacy fallback asks whether the command looks like OpenCode, which is the wrong oracle for a fixture process identified by its executable path. The genuinely shared primitives, readLinuxProcessStartTime and readPsProcessStartTime, are module-private in rpc-utils.ts, and the harness reads a procfs exe realpath rather than a command name on purpose.

The convergence worth having: export the start-time probes (procfs fast path plus ps fallback, one skew-tolerance constant) as a record-shape-agnostic helper, and have both callers layer their own identity oracle on top. That removes the duplicated ps parsing and the harness s hardcoded 5000 ms tolerance without forcing the OpenCode command heuristic into the fixture reaper.
acceptance_criteria: Both callers use one start-time probe; each keeps its own identity predicate; rpc-utils test hooks still work.
